# Phase F5a: the package-split leftovers - implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or
> superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** F5a closes the six leftovers the package split recorded. A hand-edited controller app's rows show the value
the app RUNS; the shell joins one TypeScript program; a new header-only package `n8-wire` holds the reliable link and
the expansion-volume range, so `mesen` no longer depends on `n8`; a package's VIEWS live in a module of their own, a
manifest member `retroplug.views`, which the menus never import; the controller leaves the shell and the backend by
project sections, project services, graph placers, a generic `project` host group and manifest-declared contribution
kinds; and the bundles are per product, with the DAW PLUGIN as the first product whose package list differs from the
desktop's (no `launchpad`, no `lsdj-launchpad`). **F5a changes no audio, no saved file's shape and no graph document of
any product that lists the Launchpad.** Strict parity, the kit and render baselines, `render-chunks`, `render-cli`, the
`buildGraph` and role goldens, the protocol and script digests, `edio-golden.json`, the device-check and box image
hashes and the `bliptoaster` pack's bytes hold unmodified, and no behaviour moves but the eight edges section 8 of the
design records. Exactly two records move: the recorded menu matrix's `hand-controller` case (E1, Task 1) and
`product-registrations.json`'s plugin row (E3, Task 5). Task 6 is the acceptance run.

**Architecture:** Per [modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md](modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md), whose sections 1 to 11 are
corrected in place to what the prototype built and whose section 13 records how, and
[package-split.md](package-split.md) (F5a is the first of the split's last two phases). Task 1 lands the display fix
(`controllerAppRows` reads `app.config.parse(config)`, `legacyConfigIndex` and `configRowCycler`'s index deleted, E1's
record), the `tsconfig.ui.json` fold (one shell program) and `spec/07`'s stale lines. Task 2 lands `packages/n8-wire`
(an INTERFACE target, the reliable link moved by `git mv`, `n8wire/ExpansionVolume.hpp`), `n8`'s PUBLIC link to it,
`mesen` off `n8`, the product and `retroplug_package()` lists, and two boundary fixtures. Task 3 lands the view
contract's `defineViews` and `ViewsContribution`, the `retroplug.views` member and the generated
`ui/generated/views.ts` with the moved checks, the shell's `ui/host/viewContributions.ts` and `menuDefs.ts`'s fallback
host, `lsdj`, `risa` and the fixture moved, the `ts/ui/` placement refusals in the generator and rule 3, and the
three-part pure-tier proof. Task 4 lands project sections, project services, graph placers, the `project` host group,
the contribution kinds (`defineKind`, `KIND_DATA`), the backend's harness link in the Launchpad pack, rule 9's lists
and the generic native boundary rule, so no hand-written shell source and no backend library names the Launchpad. Task
5 lands the `plugin` product list, the generator's `--product` and its per-product trees, the `onResolve` redirect, the
product-supplied bundles and their object libraries, `retroplug_product(LIST ...)`, the inverted `plugin.cmake`
assertions, the per-product checks, E3, and the docs pass including the design's as-built section. Task 6 is the
acceptance run.

**Tech stack:** no new third-party dependency: TypeScript (the workspace packages under `packages/`, the shell in
`packages/retroplug/{src,ui,cli,test,test-native,test-ui}`), the F1 package generator
(`packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs`) and the boundary check
(`packages/retroplug/scripts/check-boundaries.mjs`), esbuild through `tools/build-{controlplane,ui,session}.js` with a
new `tools/product-generated.js` redirect, pnpm's workspace links, CMake 3.28 (the product lists, the per-list bundle
targets, the boundary check) and the existing native tree. The only lockfile movement is workspace links: two
`packages/n8-wire` importers in Task 2 (the new package, and `mesen`'s and `n8`'s edges to it) and `packages/native`'s
dependency swap in Task 4 (it drops `@retroplug/launchpad` and gains devDependencies on the packs its test binaries
reach).

**Where this plan departs from the design as committed (`bef622dac`).** The design's section 13 records all of it;
this plan follows what was built. In short (a bullet quotes the record where it uses quotation marks):

- **The E1 step list rotates** (design 3.1): the recorder steps from the row's own index, so the cycler's four steps
  come in a rotated order, and the recorded case's own comment and the audit doc's prose were corrected too, since
  both asserted the old reading. The diff is still one cycler in one case: ten lines.
- **No `n8-wire` in the export tool's list, and no literal include root** (4.2): the export tool calls no
  `retroplug_package()`, and the device twin's `$<TARGET_PROPERTY:t,INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>` is transitive, so
  `retroplug-n8`'s PUBLIC link alone finds the header. **A header-only manifest, not a refused-manifest case**, and the
  boundary fixtures are `refused-native/` and `read/` (a link boundary is a target property). The wire links
  `node-sdk`'s headers target.
- **The pure proof has three entries, and the generator's fixture tree puts its UI module under `ts/ui/`** (5.2, 5.4).
  `ViewsContribution.views` is required.
- **An unstamped section reads as version 1** (6.1, decision 18); **`setSection`, `section` and `buildConfig` refuse
  core keys and `__proto__`, and a hand-edited `__proto__` key is kept as data** (6.1).
- **The section's parse is hand-written, and the pack's control-plane modules are in `ts/control/`** (6.1, 6.5,
  decision 25).
- **`ControllerSyncRule` is in the pack's placer alone, `Placement.wires` takes the protocol node's id, and `PlaceSpec`
  is core's structural type** (6.3).
- **The kind has no `idOf`, refuses an app-member name, takes the pack's whole validation in its `check`, and
  `nodeTypes` is the WIRED set** (6.5, decision 23): a type the graph does not wire is refused where the old generator
  accepted it.
- **The registry is filled by a side-effect import in `DirectGraph` and `projectConfig`** (6.3), and the literal
  scanner guards every declared node type plus a `rp.<package>.` prefix.
- **The role-golden runner alone translates `model.controller`** (6.3); `build-graph.test.ts` needs none.
- **`SHELL_IMPORTS` gains `core/defineKind`, `core/placer` and `tracker/projectService`** and loses
  `tracker/trackerPlayback` (6.6).
- **The native boundary rule is generic, not a configure check naming the Launchpad** (6.7, decision 19): the design's
  RED could not run as written because the check exempted a shell outright. `native`'s `devDependencies` gain
  `launchpad`, `n8`, `device-io` and `devtest`, and three targets are vouched for where they are made
  (`retroplug-ts-packages`, `retroplug-box-usb-cdc`, and `retroplug` against the plugin's list).
- **The harness target links `node-sdk-headers` and is declared below the device early-return** (6.7).
- **The alias claim was confirmed, so the `onResolve` plugin** (7.2, decision 17); **a product's tree resolves through a

- **No `LIST` default; a bundle set is chosen by the list's content; an unlisted `PACKAGES` is refused at configure**

- **`product-lists.mjs` exists because CMake cannot enumerate a JSON object's keys** (7.1); the subsequence rule
  refuses a duplicate by name and is a function so a fixture project can hold it; `order()` skips the shell for a

- **The typecheck's tree is `packages/retroplug/.products/`, not `build/`,** and one `tsc` runs per non-desktop list

**The behaviour edges** (design section 8, each with what was found). None changes audio, a graph document of a product
that lists the Launchpad, or a saved file's shape.

- **E1. The `hand-controller` case's `lp-app-quantise` row shows "Next bar", not "Immediately"**: the menu shows the
  value the app runs for a hand-edited `appConfig` (`quantise: 3` snaps to the schema's `bar`). `lp-app-follow` is
  unchanged, and one cycler in one recorded case is re-recorded (Task 1; the diff is the record).
- **E2. In the plugin a project with an enabled controller places no controller nodes and no sync override.** Before,
  the project's `controller.enabled` being true gave `controllerModel()` a model, so `buildGraph` placed `surface-in`,
  the controller session and `surface-out`, and forced an LSDj cart's `rp.lsdj.sync` and its serial-out twin to a mode
  of the controller's choosing (`midiMap` when the cart's SYNC was not polled or read `MidiMap`, `off` otherwise): the
  cart stopped following the DAW's MIDI clock. After F5a the plugin has no placer for the section, so nothing is
  placed and the cart syncs as its own settings say. The section is kept verbatim and written back. Held by Task 5's
  planner case against the plugin's own tree (the real-plugin render is acceptance's manual item, Task 6 Step 9).
- **E3. `product-registrations.json`'s `retroplug` row loses `rp.launchpad.surface-in` and `-out`** (Task 5): the
  two-line deletion is the record, and no other row moves.
- **E4. The plugin's bundles shrink** by 20,326 (control plane), 48,384 (UI), 21,257 (render worker) and 38,445 (script
  nodes) bytes. Sizes are no oracle (a bundle's hash moves when any bundled path moves).
- **E5. A `settings` key no package contributes is kept, not stripped**: `test/project/tolerance.test.ts`'s
  `futureSetting` expectation is the one existing test whose meaning changes, in Task 4.
- **E6. A product's script-node span labels are its positions**: in the plugin `rp.lsdj.serial-out` is 22, not 23. A
  trace name and a profile's span number only; no document, no oracle.
- **E7. The menu tests' fallback host words one refusal fewer**: not user-visible, and no test asserts either wording.
- **E8. A fresh project written by the plugin carries no `controller` block.** A section's contents come from its
  contributor's `defaults()`, and the plugin lists no package that contributes one. A `.rplg` the desktop writes opens
  in the plugin unchanged and back again; what changes is only what a project the PLUGIN creates starts with.

**The two records, and nothing else.** Never set `RP_PARITY_UPDATE`, `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_UPDATE`,
`RP_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_GRAPH_GOLDEN_UPDATE`, `RP_PLAN_BLOB_UPDATE` or `RP_SKIP_BASELINE_UPDATE`. Two variables are set
in the whole phase, both named in their step: `RP_PRODUCT_REGISTRATIONS_UPDATE=1` for E3's re-record (Task 5), whose
committed bytes are applied by hand because the dump's writer re-indents the file, and nothing else. The recorded menu
matrix moves in Task 1 by its one cycler (the diff is quoted there and the blob hash pins the result). Strict parity
(30 files, 250 cases: the suite's own count, the per-file lines' sum, while the baseline directory holds 197 entries
in 26 groups), the kit and render baselines, `render-chunks`, `render-cli`, the `buildGraph` and role goldens, the
protocol and script digests, `edio-golden.json`, both device images and the pack's bytes are this phase's proof
that nothing moved, and each task's suites step runs them. The skip baseline does not move at all (no test file is
added by a product; the moved fixture module is not a suite file). Every other existing test passes unchanged, but for
the shape changes Task 4's own steps name (a section read through `host.project`, `setModel` for `setController`,
`pollServices` for `refreshControllerSong`, and E5's one expectation). A golden, parity or digest change is a bug to
find, never a re-record.

**HARDWARE SAFETY. A real NES with an Everdrive N8 Pro, a Pico box, a probe, a Zoom L6 and MIDI interfaces are wired
in. No step in this plan may touch any of them, and these rules are absolute:**

- **Never touch the NES, the N8 cart, the Pico box or the probe**, by serial port, by USB, by a flash tool or by hand.
  The N8 tools (`n8-load`, `n8-play`, `n8-bridge`, `n8-sync`) are exercised only by their existing fake-backed tests
  (`pnpm test:n8` over fake port factories, and the native tool tests over scripted backends), and this phase changes
  no N8 wire behaviour: Task 2 moves two headers and no byte of either protocol. Every device step here happens on a
  **build**: `pnpm device:check` and `pnpm device:box` compile their images and run the check's plan in an arena, built
  and never flashed.
- **Nothing that lists or opens a system MIDI port may run, with one exception.** `pnpm sdl:controller`
  (`tools/run-sdl-controller.sh`) is that exception: it sets `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` itself, from its two ALSA fakes' full
  port names, refuses a caller that preset the variable, lists before it claims anything, and fails the run when a
  listed port is not one of its fakes. Run it as `pnpm sdl:controller`, never a bare `retroplug-sdl`, never with the
  variable preset, and never any other MIDI-port-enumerating harness. **Never touch the Zoom L6 or any MIDI interface.**
- **`pnpm sdl:smoke` runs under a scratch `RETROPLUG_USER_CONFIG_DIR` with `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW=RP_NO_PORT`, which
  matches nothing** (an EMPTY list means every port). It sets that itself; do not remove it or export a list of your
  own.
- **Never run `amidi`, `aconnect`, `aseqdump`, `aplaymidi` or any other port tool against this machine**, and never
  build or run with a saved enabled `controlSurface` in the real `~/.config/retroplug`: a saved, enabled pair is
  claimed at startup and its close bytes go out at quit, which is why the SDL tools take a scratch config dir.
- **`pnpm test`, `test:plugin`, `test:native`, `test:ui`, `device:check`, `device:box` and the CLI legs open no
  port**: their MIDI fakes are scripted openers in C++ and TypeScript. If a run seems to be waiting on MIDI, stop and
  report it rather than reaching for a queueing tool.
- `deps/sameboy` shows as modified after any configure (two tracked patches). That is expected; never stage, reset or
  stash it, and never touch any submodule (`deps/dpf.js` and everything under it included).

**Ground rules for whoever executes this:**

- This plan lives at `docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-plan.md` and is committed before Task 1 (a docs commit of its own):
  the header's links are relative to that location; every command and path in the steps is relative to the worktree
  root.
- Commit after each task (the commands are given; Task 6 commits nothing unless a step fails and is fixed, in a commit
  of its own, named for what it fixes). A commit message is a subject line, a blank line, then the body, and the
  prototype's bodies are quoted whole: use `git commit -F -` as the blocks show. No `Co-Authored-By` or "generated
  with" trailer. Do not push, and do not open a PR.
- Never use an emdash character in code, comments, docs or commit messages; use " - ", ":" or ";". Some diffs below
  carry emdashes on lines the prototype did not write (context lines of older code, the specs, and a tool's own output
  a diff quotes): leave those be. The prototype's own passes removed every emdash from an added line.
- Run every command from the worktree root with absolute paths or a subshell (`(cd x && ...)`); never `cd` the session
  itself. Never bare `git stash`, never switch branches with uncommitted work in the tree, and never `rm -rf build` to
  fix CMake: investigate.
- **Every whole-file block below (a `Create`) is followed by the `sed -n` range that extracts it from this plan and by
  the blob hash the file must have:** write or extract the file, then `git hash-object <path>` must print the hash the
  step quotes, which is the prototype commit's blob. **Every diff block is followed by its extraction, a
  `git apply --check`, and the blob hash of each file it changes**, so an applied diff is the prototype's bytes and not
  just something that applies. The temporary `patch` blocks are the RED proofs that need the old code: each is applied,
  run, and reversed by the step after it. A RED whose "before" is another tree is derived from a `git archive` instead,
  and the step says which.
- **The generated modules are never committed.** `packages/retroplug/src/generated/{packages,consoles,protocol,
  scriptNodes,placers}.ts`, `packages/retroplug/ui/generated/{menus,views}.ts`,
  `packages/retroplug/cli/generated/tools.ts`, `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.host-modules.json`,
  `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.paths.json` and, from Task 5, the per-product trees under `build/products/` and
  `packages/retroplug/.products/` are written by the generator and gitignored, and the runners, `pnpm typecheck` and
  the CMake `retroplug-ts-packages[-<product>]` targets regenerate them. A worktree a prototype build ran in holds all
  of them, untracked and ignored (this one does); no `git status` list below shows them. If one ever does,
  `.gitignore` is wrong: stop and report it.
- **The lockfile moves in TWO tasks, and only by workspace links.** Task 2 adds `packages/n8-wire` and the two edges
  to it, so it runs `pnpm install --offline` (the prototype's command: **not** `--frozen-lockfile`, and never a bare
  re-resolve that prunes another platform's optional packages) and quotes the whole `pnpm-lock.yaml` diff, which is one
  of its diff blocks; Task 4 drops `packages/native`'s `@retroplug/launchpad` and adds its devDependencies, the same
  way. Tasks 1, 3 and 5 add no dependency and run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, checking the lockfile's
  blob.
- **Case counts are exact. Assertion totals are exact too, with three exceptions:** a run of
  `retroplug-engine-graph-test` reports a total that moves from run to run (its threaded cases assert in loops), and so
  do `retroplug-launchpad-test`'s and the ThreadSanitizer run of `[script-pack]`; for those the case count must match
  and the total is the prototype's, quoted for scale. Catch2 pads its `test cases:` columns with spaces, which the
  quotes below collapse to one. `pnpm test`'s final line counts FILES; a case total is quoted from a report or a
  compare line and is not the runner's own line, and the `jobs=N` a runner prints is the pool it was given (the kit's
  caps), not a figure to match.
- **The Catch2 binaries and `retroplug-render-host-test` are `EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL` or outside the default build:**
  `cmake --build build` does not rebuild them, so a library edit needs the target built by name before a run
  (`pnpm test:plugin`, `test:n8` and `test:native` build theirs first, and the render-host tool is built by name).
  **A manifest change, a CMake list change or a new package needs `cmake -S . -B build` first** (the generator's
  inputs, the product lists and every new target are configure-time), which is why Tasks 2, 4 and 5 configure before
  they build.
- **The scratch root, and one filesystem rule.** Every scratch path this plan writes is under `/tmp/f5a-accept`,
  `/tmp/f5a-tree-<n>` or `/tmp/f5a-v*`; none is inside the repository. The per-task and fresh-archive recipes run
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` in the tree and give the pure runner the worktree's tjs binary through
  `RETROPLUG_TJS`; **a task's extracted tree never links this worktree's `build/`**, because a run that wrote there
  would write into this worktree. Do not `cp -al node_modules` into a scratch tree either (a hardlink cannot cross a
  filesystem, and a plain symlink makes pnpm's per-package links resolve back into this worktree).
- The build trees were last built at the prototype's tip, so each task's first build recompiles what changed and
  regenerates the generated modules; that is expected. Task 5's build also makes the plugin's per-product tree and its
  bundles, and Task 6 rebuilds all of it and hashes the images from the dirs it made.
- **When a step's result differs from its Expected, stop and report.** A different exit status, case count or quoted
  text is a finding. Three exceptions: an assertion total the rule above calls moving; a predicted failure whose
  failing file, case or target is the one predicted but whose wording differs (the red steps say which are predicted);
  and a device script's trap-probe lines, whose object path and offsets are this devcontainer's and this binutils' (the
  device scripts judge a probe by its own object and the two symbol names, `__wrap__Znwj` and `__wrap_malloc`). Never
  edit code, a test or a golden to make a step pass. In Tasks 1 to 5 each task's tree must equal its prototype commit,
  so a real defect found there is reported, not fixed; a fix belongs to a commit of its own after the plan.
- **Track progress outside the committed plan:** never tick its checkboxes. Ticking one modifies
  `docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-plan.md`, and every task's expected `git status` list would then gain a line it does
  not show.
- The Windows build has not seen this tree (the prototype is local and Linux-only), so an MSVC-only warning or error is
  a real finding to report, not a stale quote: Task 6 states the owed items, and no step below builds on Windows. macOS
  and the arm64 Linux CI job have not run either. **No step below needs a real device, and none may touch one.**

**Commit this plan before Task 1.** Before the commit, check where the tree is: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` must
print `feature/modularize`, `git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD` must print `bef622da`, and
`git status --short --untracked-files=all` must show ` m deps/sameboy` and nothing else (the generated modules are
ignored, so they do not appear). If the branch or the commit differs, stop: every step below assumes the design commit
on a tree with nothing else in it. (`git -C deps/sameboy status --short` shows the five files the two tracked SameBoy
patches change: `Core/apu.c`, `Core/apu.h`, `Core/camera.c`, `Core/random.c` and `Core/sgb.c`.) The run below copies

### Task 1: the app rows show what the app runs, and the UI joins one shell program

Design sections 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 8 (E1), and the design's first stage. Three small fixes: a controller app's rows
read the value the app RUNS instead of the project's literal `appConfig`, `tsconfig.ui.json` folds into the shell's one
program, and `spec/07`'s stale lines are corrected. One record moves (E1: the recorded menu matrix's `hand-controller`
case, one cycler), and nothing else in the phase does.

The stage ran in two passes: the fix, the fold and the docs, then a fix pass that made the fake-app case earn its place
(a `toggle` knob defaulting `false` and a `range` knob past its bound, each shown RED), restored `spec/07`'s two shape
questions with credits, and corrected four comments. Both passes are this commit, so the plan places the final files and
the RED it quotes is the one the pass recorded.

**Files:**

- Modify (13 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 4 under `packages/retroplug/test/menu/`; 2 under `packages/retroplug/`; 1 under `docs/`; 1 under `packages/launchpad/ts/`; 1 under `packages/launchpad/ts/ui/`; 1 under `packages/retroplug/ui/types/` and the rest)
- Delete (1): `packages/retroplug/tsconfig.ui.json`

- [ ] **Step 1: The RED: the two cases against the old reading**

The test file is the commit's, run against the tree's OLD sources: `packages/launchpad/ts/ui/index.ts`'s
`controllerAppRows` reads `legacyConfigIndex(field, current(field.key))`, which is index 0 for a value the schema
snaps, and `packages/ui/ts/contribution.ts` still has `legacyConfigIndex`. Both cases fail, and the failure lines are
the proof that the parse is what moves. The first case is MI.MAP's own `quantise` knob (its default `bar` is index 2
of four, so a stored `{ quantise: "whenever" }` shows "Next bar" under the fix); the second registers a fake app under
MI.MAP's id, restored in a `finally`, whose `toggle` defaults `false` and whose `range` is clamped to 0..10 with a
step table running to 15, which is the only shape where the literal and parsed readings differ for a range.

- [ ] **Step 2: The fix: the rows read the same parse the runtime gets**

`controllerAppRows` builds `running = app.config.parse(config)` and `defaults = app.config.parse({})` and reads each
knob from `running[field.key]` with `defaults[field.key]` still the wrong-type fallback: exactly what
`parseAppConfig(app.id, config)` hands the runtime (`app.config.parse(config ?? {})`). A range row never had a legacy
reading, and a `toggle` knob whose schema default is `false` also changes display (the old reading showed On for any
stored value but `false`; `boolField(false)` snaps a non-boolean to `false`), which no shipped app has: MI.MAP's
`follow` defaults `true`, where both readings are On, so E1 stays exactly the one cycler. `legacyConfigIndex` is
deleted with its doc comments, and `configRowCycler` loses its `index` parameter, whose only caller it was.
`rows.test.ts`'s comment loses the deleted name.

### Task 2: `n8-wire`, and `mesen` off `n8`

Design section 4 and the design's second stage. BlipToaster's reliable link and the expansion-volume range are what a
real N8 Pro cart and the emulated NES FIFO that stands in for it have to agree on, and neither package owns them, so
they move into a new header-only package `packages/n8-wire`: `transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp` by `git mv` (its include
path unchanged, so its four includers do not change) and `n8wire/ExpansionVolume.hpp`, holding the three constants out
of `n8/N8Node.hpp`, which now includes it. `rp::n8::expansionVolumeRegister` stays in `n8`: only the cart's side
rescales the percent. `n8` and `mesen` both declare the package and neither declares the other.

The package is the header-only manifest form the reader already accepts (`retroplug.native` naming a target and no
entry), and its target links `retroplug-node-sdk-headers` alone: the link is headers and needs no library of the SDK's.
It joins the root desktop list and the two device builds' `retroplug_package()` lists, and joins no DEVICE product's
`PACKAGES`: a device product refuses a package with no `device` entry, which the prototype verified and this task
quotes.

**Files:**

- Create (5): `packages/n8-wire/native/CMakeLists.txt`, `packages/n8-wire/native/src/n8wire/ExpansionVolume.hpp`, `packages/n8-wire/package.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/read/MesenN8WireDeclared.json`, `packages/native/test/packages/refused-native/N8WireUndeclared.json`
- Move (1 file, each by the `git mv` its step prints; byte identical): from `packages/n8/native/src/transport/`
- Modify (16 files, as one diff block per group its step names: 1 under `package.json`; 1 under `packages/graph-runtime/device-check/`; 1 under `packages/mesen/native/`; 1 under `packages/mesen/native/src/system/mesen/`; 1 under `packages/mesen/native/test/`; 1 under `packages/mesen/` and the rest)

- [ ] **Step 1: The package, and the link moved**

`packages/n8-wire/package.json` says what the package is (the wire a real cart and the emulated NES FIFO share) and
what "device-ready" means here: the range is compiled by every device build through `rp.n8.nes` (`N8Node.cpp` includes
it), while the link is compiled by no device target and its `std::function` emit may allocate, so it is device-ready
by inspection, not by a check. `native/CMakeLists.txt` is an `INTERFACE` target with `native/src` as its root, linking
`retroplug-node-sdk-headers` for `util/FixedQueue.hpp` and nothing of the SDK's library. `ExpansionVolume.hpp` holds
`kExpansionVolumeMin = 0`, `Max = 200` and `Default = 100` in `namespace rp::n8`, the names they had, heap-free. The
reliable link moves with `git mv` and is byte identical (100% similar): its include path is what its four includers
spell, so none of them changes.

Create `packages/n8-wire/package.json`:

````json
{
  "name": "@retroplug/n8-wire",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,

Two headers and no code; `device-ready` here says what is checked: the range is compiled by every device build, through rp.n8.nes, while the link is compiled by no device target and its std::function emit may allocate, so the link is device-ready by inspection, not by a check.",
  "dependencies": {
    "@retroplug/node-sdk": "workspace:*"
  },
  "retroplug": {
    "native": { "target": "retroplug-n8-wire" }
  }
}
````

Create `packages/n8-wire/native/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# The N8 wire (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 4): what a real Everdrive N8 Pro cart and the emulated
# NES FIFO that stands in for it have to agree on, and what neither owns - BlipToaster's reliable link, the one sender
# (rp::N8ReliableSender) each side drives over its own transport: the cart's desktop link (packages/n8's N8Link) in wall
# time, the emulator's FIFO role (packages/mesen's NesN8FifoRole) in emulated CPU time - and the expansion-volume range
# the emulated chip and the cart's master-volume register are both set from. Added by retroplug_package(n8-wire)
# (cmake/packages.cmake); `n8` and `mesen` both list it and neither lists the other, so the console and the cartridge
# meet at a package that is nobody's own.
#
# Header-only, so an INTERFACE target: a consumer gets this package's include root, where the two headers keep the paths
# they are included by ("transport/N8ReliableLink.hpp", "n8wire/ExpansionVolume.hpp"), and node-sdk's include root, for
# the link's frame store (util/FixedQueue.hpp, header-only: nothing here links reflect-cpp or any library). A device build
# adds it too, between node-sdk and the packages that list it.
add_library(retroplug-n8-wire INTERFACE)
target_include_directories(retroplug-n8-wire INTERFACE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src)
target_link_libraries(retroplug-n8-wire INTERFACE retroplug-node-sdk-headers)
````

````cpp
// The expansion-volume range rp.mesen.nes and rp.n8.nes share (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 4): whole
````

`retroplug-mesen` links `retroplug-n8-wire` where it linked `retroplug-n8`, and its header comment says the wire is
nobody's own; `retroplug-n8` links `retroplug-n8-wire` PUBLIC, which alone is what finds `n8wire/ExpansionVolume.hpp`
(a target's `INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES` carries a linked INTERFACE target's roots, and the device twin copies that
property). `pico/n8-host/CMakeLists.txt` and `packages/graph-runtime/device-check/CMakeLists.txt` each gain
`retroplug_package(n8-wire)` before `n8`, because those are the lists that call `retroplug_package()` in a device
build. The export tool's list gains nothing: it calls no `retroplug_package()` (its device objects are the desktop
build's `<target>-device` twins, which exist because `n8-wire` is in the root desktop list), and its
`RP_EXPORT_PLAN_PACKAGES` is a DEVICE product's list, which must not carry the package.

### Task 3: a package's views are their own module, apart from the menus

Design section 5 and the design's third stage. A package's views move out of `defineUi`: `@retroplug/ui/contribution`
gains `defineViews` and `ViewsContribution` beside `defineUi`, `UiContribution` keeps rows, menus, trackers, services and
actions and loses `views`, and a package declares a views module with the new manifest member `retroplug.views`,
published at `./views`. The generator reads it as it reads `ui` and writes `ui/generated/views.ts`: the contributions,
the flattened table and the view checks moved whole out of `renderMenus` with their state, while `menus.ts` keeps the
rows, the trackers, the services, the builder placements and the actions. The shell's view readers move to
`ui/host/viewContributions.ts`, and `menuDefs.ts`'s fallback host imports no view function (E7).

The stage's cause is held RED: before the split, a package's React view in its `ui` module made the generated menus
module fail to bundle with the pure runner's options, so the first product to list a React view package would have
broken the pure tier. The proof is three cases over a Node driver: the fixture's views module bundles as the UI bundle
bundles it, the pure tier's three menu modules carry no view and no kit, and a generated menus module never reaches a
React view while a generated views module does.

The stage ran in two passes: the split, then a fix pass that made `menuDefs.ts` the third pure entry, made `zeta`
views-only in the generator's fixture tree, put `views.ts` in the CMake byproducts, and shared one fixture alias map
between the two drivers. Both passes are this commit.

- [ ] **Step 2: The generator: the member, the generated module, and the checks moved**

`contributions()` reads `retroplug.views` as it reads `retroplug.ui`, `contributes()` counts it, and `renderViews`
writes `ui/generated/views.ts` with `VIEW_CONTRIBUTIONS`, the flattened `VIEWS` and `checkView` with its state
(`viewOwners`, `viewPlacements`, `bodyKinds`) moved whole out of `renderMenus`: a view id declared twice in one
package or two; a placement that is neither `window` nor `tile`; a body `kind` that is none of `pixels`, `readout`,
`component`; a `pixels` or `readout` body with no `open`, a `component` body with no `component` function; a `visible`
on a window view; and the cross-package duplicate. `menus.ts` keeps `UI_CONTRIBUTIONS`, `ACTIONS`, the row/tracker/
service/builder/action checks and loses `VIEWS`, the view check and the `ViewDef` import. The generated module reads
`views.views ?? []`, so a plain-data fixture module cannot crash it before a check speaks. Two refusals join it, each
naming the package and the path: a `retroplug.views` path outside the package's `ts/ui/` tree, because rule 3 admits a
React host module only from there and a views module outside it could import React with nothing checking it; and the
same refusal for `retroplug.ui`, which had never had one (every `ui` entry in the tree is `ts/ui/index.ts`, so no
manifest moves). `packages/native/cmake/bundles.cmake` records `ui/generated/views.ts` among the generator's
byproducts, as it records `menus.ts`.

- [ ] **Step 4: The shell: the view readers apart from the menu readers**

`ui/host/viewContributions.ts` holds `viewById`, `windowViewOf`, `windowViewOrReport` and `tileViews` over
`../generated/views`; `menuContributions.ts` keeps the menu and action functions over `../generated/menus` alone.
`App.tsx` and `TileViews.tsx` take the view functions from the new module. **`menuDefs.ts` is the load-bearing one:**
it stops importing a view function, and its fallback host's `views.open` reports only "the menu's host has no window
to open <id> in" (E7), because importing `viewContributions` would pull the generated views module, and with it a
component view's React, into every pure-tier test that reaches this file. No test asserts either wording, and the
reference counts of the two files are unchanged.

Create `packages/retroplug/ui/host/viewContributions.ts`:

````ts
// The product's views (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 5.3), for the shell's view slots: the generated
// views module, in product order, is the one place a package's views are read from. Apart from menuContributions' menus
// module on purpose: a component view imports React, and only the UI bundle resolves it, so a menu module that reached
// this one would put React in every pure-tier test that builds a menu.
import type { TileView, ViewDef, WindowView } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { VIEWS } from "../generated/views";

/** The view a package registers under `id`, with the package it came from, or undefined. The generated module has
 *  already refused a duplicate id, so the first match is the only one. */
export function viewById(id: string): { pkg: string; view: ViewDef } | undefined {
  return VIEWS.find((entry) => entry.view.id === id);
}

/** The window view a package registers under `id`, or undefined for an unknown id or a tile view. What
 *  `host.views.open` looks an id up in, so a tile view's id opens nothing. */
export function windowViewOf(id: string): WindowView | undefined {
  const entry = viewById(id);
  return entry?.view.placement === "window" ? entry.view : undefined;
}

/** Resolve a window open against the generated registry: the view, or the report saying why it cannot open. App's
 *  `views.open` runs this and then the two checks only a project can answer (a system that is gone, a view whose `when`
 *  rejects it), so the id's own refusals are worded in one place. */
export function windowViewOrReport(id: string): { view: WindowView } | { report: string } {
  const entry = viewById(id);
  if (!entry) return { report: `[views] no view is registered under the id ${id}` };
  if (entry.view.placement !== "window") return { report: `[views] ${id} is a tile view, which opens no window` };
  return { view: entry.view };
}

/** Every tile view, in product order, with the package it came from: the layers EmulatorTile mounts over each tile
 *  whose system the view's `when` accepts. */
export function tileViews(): readonly { pkg: string; view: TileView }[] {
  return VIEWS.filter((entry): entry is { pkg: string; view: TileView } => entry.view.placement === "tile");
}
````

- [ ] **Step 5: The packages' views: `lsdj`, `risa` and the fixture**

`lsdj/ts/ui/views.ts` is `export default defineViews({ views: [hdView, overlayView] })`, `risa`'s is the overlay
alone, and each `index.ts` drops the two imports and the `views` line, keeping `trackers` and `actions`
(`lsdjDebugOverlay` is an action; the overlay's `visible` flag is the shared `debugOverlay.ts` signal). `ui-fixture`
becomes a views-only package: its manifest drops `ui` and gains `views`, its `ts/ui/index.ts` goes and
`ts/ui/views.ts` holds `defineViews({ views: [badgeView] })`, and its `exports` publishes `./views`. Each moved
package's `exports` gains `./views` (no wildcard). `hdView.ts`, `overlayView.ts`, `Badge.tsx` and the two
`debugOverlay.ts` are byte identical.

Create `packages/lsdj/ts/ui/views.ts`:

````ts
// LSDj's views (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 5.3), apart from its UI contribution: the HD player's
// full-window screen and the debug readout over every tile. They are a manifest member of their own (`retroplug.views`)
// because only the UI bundle may carry a package's views - the pure tier bundles the menu modules with no alias, so a
// module that imports React would break every menu test - and neither view imports anything of the shell's.
import { defineViews } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { hdView } from "./hdView";
import { overlayView } from "./overlayView";

export default defineViews({ views: [hdView, overlayView] });
````

````ts
// @retroplug/ui-fixture's views module: the component view a package's React half is proved by, and nothing else (the
// package declares `retroplug.views` and no `ui` contribution, which a package may).
//
// The package is listed by no product, so nothing here reaches a product's bundle (the views split's proof bundles it
// alone, as the UI bundle would): it is the worked example spec/06's "a view" step copies, and the shape rule 3's
// refusals are copies of (a .tsx under ts/ui/, the React host modules its files import declared in the manifest, and a
// tsconfig that extends the generated host-module paths).
import { defineViews, type TileView } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import { reactView } from "@retroplug/ui-react";

import { Badge } from "./Badge";

export { Badge };

/** The tile view this package contributes, built the way the kit asks: a component body. `satisfies` is what the
 *  contract checks here, since the view is declared as data rather than through a helper of its own. */
export const badgeView = {
  id: "ui-fixture-badge",
  label: "Fixture Badge",
  placement: "tile",
  body: reactView(Badge),
} satisfies TileView;

/** The package's contribution: the view it adds and nothing of the rows, menus, trackers, services or actions. */
export default defineViews({ views: [badgeView] });
````

````ts
// Generated by packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs from the desktop product's package list and the
// packages' manifests. Do not edit; edit a manifest and rebuild.
//
// The product's views, in product order: each package's `retroplug.views` module, default-exporting the window
// and tile views it draws. Only the shell's view slots import this module, and only the UI bundle resolves it: a
// component view imports React, which the pure tier (the menu tests, the control plane, the CLI) has no path to.
import type { ViewDef, ViewsContribution } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";
import views_zeta from "@retroplug/zeta/views";

/** Each package's views, in product order. */
export const VIEW_CONTRIBUTIONS: readonly { pkg: string; views: ViewsContribution }[] = [
  { pkg: "zeta", views: views_zeta },
];

/** The product's views, in product order, with the package each came from: what host.views.open looks
 *  a window view up by id, and the tile layers every tile mounts in turn. */
export const VIEWS: readonly { pkg: string; view: ViewDef }[] = VIEW_CONTRIBUTIONS.flatMap(({ pkg, views }) =>
  (views.views ?? []).map((view) => ({ pkg, view })),
);

// A view's id is its test id and the id host.views.open names, so it is unique across the product; its
// placement and its body's kind are the two data fields the type cannot hold a package to at load.
const viewOwners = new Map<string, string>();
const viewPlacements = new Set<string>(["window", "tile"]);
const bodyKinds = new Set<string>(["pixels", "readout", "component"]);

/** One contributed view: its id unique across the product, its placement one the shell has, its body kind
 *  one the shell renders with what that kind is opened by (a session's `open`, a component's `component`), and
 *  no `visible` on a window view (the type refuses that; this backs the type). */
function checkView(pkg: string, view: ViewDef): void {
  const owner = viewOwners.get(view.id);
  if (owner !== undefined) {
    throw new Error(owner === pkg
      ? `the package ${pkg} declares the view ${view.id} twice`
      : `two packages declare the view ${view.id}: ${owner} and ${pkg}`);
  }
  viewOwners.set(view.id, pkg);
  if (!viewPlacements.has(view.placement)) {
    throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares the view ${view.id} at the placement ${view.placement}, ` +
      `which is no placement (the placements are window, tile)`);
  }
  const kind = view.body?.kind;
  if (!bodyKinds.has(kind)) {
    throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares the view ${view.id} with the body kind ${kind}, ` +
      `which is no body kind (the kinds are pixels, readout, component)`);
  }
  const body = view.body as { readonly open?: unknown; readonly component?: unknown };
  if (kind === "component") {
    if (typeof body.component !== "function") {
      throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares the view ${view.id} with a component body and no ` +
        "component (reactView builds the one a component body carries)");
    }
  } else if (typeof body.open !== "function") {
    throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares the view ${view.id} with a ${kind} body and no open ` +
      `(a ${kind} body's open is what the shell calls)`);
  }
  if (view.placement !== "tile" && (view as { readonly visible?: unknown }).visible !== undefined) {
    throw new Error(`the package ${pkg} declares the window view ${view.id} with a visible flag, which only ` +
      `a tile view has`);
  }
}

for (const { pkg, views } of VIEW_CONTRIBUTIONS) {
  for (const view of views.views ?? []) checkView(pkg, view);
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/packages/fixtureAliases.mjs`:

````js
// The aliases a bundle of the generator's fixture tree needs, in one place: test/packages/run-generator.mjs bundles
// the fixture tree's generated modules to run their checks, and test/script/bundle-views.mjs bundles them to prove
// the views split, and the two must name the same files or the second would test a tree the first does not.
//
// A fixture tree lives outside the workspace, so nothing stands in for the pnpm links a real build resolves: each
// fixture package's contribution is aliased by the specifier its manifest exports, the ui contract by the real one, and
// the fixture shell's src/*.ts shims by the real shell's binding vocabulary (an action's defaults are then checked
// against the real key names, pad names and shell defaults rather than against a copy of them). React is aliased by
// none of them, which is what the views split's absence case rests on.
import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const SHELL = resolve(HERE, "../..");

/** The alias map for a fixture tree at `root`. */
export function fixtureAliases(root) {
  return {
    "@retroplug/alpha/app": join(root, "packages/alpha/ts/app.ts"),
    "@retroplug/beta/app": join(root, "packages/beta/ts/app.ts"),
    "@retroplug/alpha/consoles": join(root, "packages/alpha/ts/consoles.ts"),
    "@retroplug/beta/consoles": join(root, "packages/beta/ts/consoles.ts"),
    "@retroplug/alpha/ui": join(root, "packages/alpha/ts/ui/index.ts"),
    "@retroplug/beta/ui": join(root, "packages/beta/ts/ui/index.ts"),
    "@retroplug/zeta/ui": join(root, "packages/zeta/ts/ui/index.ts"),
    "@retroplug/alpha/views": join(root, "packages/alpha/ts/ui/views.ts"),
    "@retroplug/beta/views": join(root, "packages/beta/ts/ui/views.ts"),
    "@retroplug/zeta/views": join(root, "packages/zeta/ts/ui/views.ts"),
    // The ui package itself is a workspace dependency of the shell, not a fixture package: a real build resolves it
    // through the pnpm link, so the caller hands the bundle the tree's own copy.
    "@retroplug/ui/contribution": join(SHELL, "../ui/ts/contribution.ts"),
    "@retroplug/shell/keyCodes": join(SHELL, "src/keyCodes.ts"),
    "@retroplug/shell/bindingMap": join(SHELL, "src/bindingMap.ts"),
  };
}
````

- [ ] **Step 7: The pure-tier proof**

`test/script/bundle-views.mjs` is a Node driver beside `bundle-split.mjs`, and `bundle-view-package.test.ts` has three
cases over it: (1) the fixture's views module bundles with `uiBuildOptions` and `bundleInputs` from
`tools/build-ui.js` (the kit's aliases, the dpf.js `nodePaths`, `jsx: "automatic"`), and its inputs include
`packages/ui-react/` and a `react` module; (2) the real `ui/generated/menus.ts`, `ui/host/menuContributions.ts` and
`ui/screens/menu/menuDefs.ts` bundle with the pure runner's own options (`platform: "neutral"`, no alias) and their
inputs contain no `ui/generated/views`, no package's views module and nothing under `packages/ui-react/`; (3) a
fixture tree whose views module imports `react` generates a `menus.ts` that still bundles while its `views.ts` fails
with `Could not resolve "react"`, asserted as the expected failure. `bundle-ui-split.test.ts` adds one case: the UI
bundle carries the generated view table and no other bundle does.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/script/bundle-views.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// The driver behind test/script/bundle-view-package.test.ts (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 5.4): the
// three bundles that prove the views split, each built in memory and reported as the modules that went in.
//
//   node test/script/bundle-views.mjs fixture-view   the fixture package's views module, as the UI bundle builds it
//   node test/script/bundle-views.mjs pure           the shell's menu and views modules, as the pure tier bundles them
//   node test/script/bundle-views.mjs views-react    a fixture tree whose views module imports react, generated and
//                                                    bundled both ways
//
// The build is Node's (esbuild is not a txiki module), so the test runs this in a node child, as bundle-split.mjs runs
// the surface bundles.
import { cpSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { fixtureAliases } from "../packages/fixtureAliases.mjs";

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const { esbuild } = require("../../../../tools/esbuild-shared");
const { uiBuildOptions } = require("../../../../tools/build-ui.js");
const { generate } = await import("../../scripts/lib/packages.mjs");

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const SHELL = resolve(HERE, "../..");
const REPO = resolve(SHELL, "../..");
const MODE = process.argv[2];

/** The options the pure tier bundles a test with (scripts/run-tests.mjs): platform neutral, no alias, and nothing of
 *  the UI bundle's nodePaths, so React is not resolvable. A copy of run-tests.mjs:122-135, which a test cannot import;
 *  keep the two in step. `root` is esbuild's working directory for the fixture-tree case, whose entry lives outside the
 *  repository. */
function pureOptions(entry, root) {
  return {
    entryPoints: [entry],
    bundle: true,
    format: "esm",
    platform: "neutral",
    mainFields: ["module", "main"],
    target: "es2020",
    absWorkingDir: root,
    outfile: join(root, "bundle.js"),
    define: { "process.env.NODE_ENV": '"production"' },
    metafile: true,
  };
}

/** Build `entry` in memory and report the modules that went in (absolute, forward slashes) or the one error. */
function bundle(options) {
  try {
    const result = esbuild.buildSync({ ...options, write: false });
    return { inputs: Object.keys(result.metafile.inputs).map((input) => resolve(options.absWorkingDir, input)) };
  } catch (e) {
    const errors = (e.errors ?? []).map((error) => error.text);
    return { error: errors.length ? errors.join("; ") : String(e) };
  }
}


const result = (() => {
  switch (MODE) {
    case "fixture-view":
      // A view package as the UI bundle builds it: tools/build-ui.js's own options, which alias lvgljs and lvgljs-ui,
      // point nodePaths at the dpf.js React and turn JSX on.
      return bundle(uiBuildOptions(resolve(SHELL, "../ui-fixture/ts/ui/views.ts"), join(REPO, "build/ui/views.js")));
    case "pure": {
      // The three modules the pure tier reaches when it builds a menu, bundled as a test is: no alias. The menus
      // module, the menu composer and the menu definitions (the file about 25 menu tests enter through) must carry
      // neither the generated views module nor a package's views, so a module that re-imported a view function would
      // be caught here rather than only by the first product to list a React view package.
      return {
        menus: bundle(pureOptions(join(SHELL, "ui/generated/menus.ts"), SHELL)),
        composer: bundle(pureOptions(join(SHELL, "ui/host/menuContributions.ts"), SHELL)),
        defs: bundle(pureOptions(join(SHELL, "ui/screens/menu/menuDefs.ts"), SHELL)),
      };
    }
    case "views-react": {
      // A fixture tree whose package contributes a views module that imports react: the generated menus module must
      // still bundle with the pure options (it never reaches a view), and the generated views module must not. That is
      // the cause of the split, held as a failing case rather than a comment.
      const work = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "rp-views-"));
      try {
        const root = join(work, "tree");
        cpSync(join(HERE, "../packages/fixtures/tree"), root, { recursive: true });
        mkdirSync(join(root, "packages/alpha/ts/ui"), { recursive: true });
        const viewsFile = join(root, "packages/alpha/ts/ui/views.ts");
        writeFileSync(
          viewsFile,
          'import { createElement } from "react";\n' +
            'import { defineViews } from "@retroplug/ui/contribution";\n' +
            'export default defineViews({ views: [{ id: "alpha-react", label: "Alpha React", placement: "tile", ' +
            'body: { kind: "component", component: () => createElement("box", null) } }] });\n',
        );
        const manifest = join(root, "packages/alpha/package.json");
        const json = JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifest, "utf8"));
        json.retroplug.views = "ts/ui/views.ts";
        json.exports["./views"] = "./ts/ui/views.ts";
        writeFileSync(manifest, `${JSON.stringify(json, null, 2)}\n`);
        generate({ root });
        const options = (entry) => ({ ...pureOptions(entry, root), alias: fixtureAliases(root) });
        return {
          menus: bundle(options(join(root, "packages/retroplug/ui/generated/menus.ts"))),
          views: bundle(options(join(root, "packages/retroplug/ui/generated/views.ts"))),
        };
      } finally {
        rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true });
      }
    }
    default:
      console.error(`bundle-views.mjs: unknown mode "${MODE}"`);
      process.exit(2);
  }
})();

process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(result));
````

Create `packages/retroplug/test/script/bundle-view-package.test.ts`:

````ts
// The pure-tier proof of the views split (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 5.4): a package's views are UI
// code, and the shell's menu modules are not. Before the split, ui/generated/menus.ts imported every package's `ui`
// module, so the first product to list a React view package would have broken every pure-tier test that reaches
// menuDefs.ts, because the runner bundles with no aliases and no React path. Three cases hold the two halves apart:
//
// 1. a view package bundles as the UI bundle bundles it: with tools/build-ui.js's aliases, nodePaths and JSX, the
//    fixture package's views module carries @retroplug/ui-react and React itself;
// 2. the pure tier's modules (ui/host/menuContributions.ts, the generated menus.ts and ui/screens/menu/menuDefs.ts, the
//    file the menu tests enter through) bundle with the runner's own options and carry no generated views module, no
//    package's views and nothing of the kit;
// 3. the cause, held as a case: a fixture tree whose views module imports react generates a menus module that bundles
//    without it (and a views module that does not), which is the failure the pre-split generator produced for the
//    menus module itself.
//
// The build is Node's, so test/script/bundle-views.mjs runs it in a child, as bundle-split.mjs runs the surface
// bundles.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";

// Just enough of txiki's spawn and a child's pipe, declared locally as bundle-split.test.ts declares them.
interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

interface BundleReport {
  inputs?: string[];
  error?: string;
}

/** One driver mode's report, with every input path made forward-slashed (a Windows build's metafile paths are). */
async function drive(mode: string): Promise<any> {
  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "test/script/bundle-views.mjs", mode], {
    stdout: "pipe",
    stderr: "pipe",
  });
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  if (status.term_signal || status.exit_status !== 0) {
    throw new Error(`the view bundle driver failed: ${err || out}`);
  }
  return JSON.parse(out) as Record<string, any>;
}

/** A report's inputs as forward-slashed paths, or the failure reported beside them. */
function inputsOf(report: BundleReport): string[] {
  if (report.error !== undefined) throw new Error(`the bundle failed: ${report.error}`);
  return (report.inputs ?? []).map((path) => path.split("\\").join("/"));
}

const isKit = (path: string): boolean => /\/packages\/ui-react\//.test(path);
const isReact = (path: string): boolean => /\/node_modules\/react\//.test(path);
/** A package's views module, or the shell's generated view table. */
const isViews = (path: string): boolean =>
  /\/ui\/generated\/views\.ts$/.test(path) || /\/packages\/[^/]+\/ts\/ui\/views\.ts$/.test(path);

test("a view package bundles as the UI bundle bundles it: the kit and React itself", async () => {
  const inputs = inputsOf((await drive("fixture-view")) as BundleReport);
  const kit = inputs.filter(isKit);
  const react = inputs.filter(isReact);
  console.log(`# fixture-view: ${inputs.length} modules, ${kit.length} kit, ${react.length} React`);
  expect(kit.length > 0, "the view package's bundle carries no @retroplug/ui-react module").toBe(true);
  expect(react.length > 0, "the view package's bundle carries no React module").toBe(true);
});

test("the pure tier's menu modules carry no view and no kit", async () => {
  const report = await drive("pure");
  for (const name of ["menus", "composer", "defs"] as const) {
    const inputs = inputsOf(report[name] as BundleReport);
    const views = inputs.filter(isViews);
    const kit = inputs.filter(isKit);
    console.log(`# pure ${name}: ${inputs.length} modules, ${views.length} views, ${kit.length} kit`);
    expect(views, `the pure ${name} bundle carries a views module`).toEqual([]);
    expect(kit, `the pure ${name} bundle carries @retroplug/ui-react`).toEqual([]);
  }
  // The positive control: the generated menu table IS carried by the two modules that read it, so the case is not
  // vacuous (the menus module is the table itself).
  for (const name of ["menus", "composer"] as const) {
    expect(
      inputsOf(report[name] as BundleReport).some((path) => /\/ui\/generated\/menus\.ts$/.test(path)),
      `the pure ${name} bundle carries no generated menus module`,
    ).toBe(true);
  }
});

test("a generated menus module never reaches a React view, and a generated views module does", async () => {
  const report = await drive("views-react");
  // The menus module of a tree whose package contributes a React view still bundles with the pure options: it reaches
  // the package's `ui` module alone.
  const menus = inputsOf(report.menus as BundleReport);
  expect(menus.some(isViews)).toBe(false);
  // And the views module that tree generated needs React, which the pure tier has no path to: asserted as the expected
  // failure, so the split cannot be undone silently.
  const views = report.views as BundleReport;
  console.log(`# views-react: menus ${menus.length} modules; views: ${views.error}`);
  expect(views.inputs).toBe(undefined);
  expect((views.error ?? "").includes('Could not resolve "react"')).toBe(true);
});
````

````text
  ok: nothing selected, nothing claimed; unclaimed, the device's notes reach the shared stream
  ok: reclaimed before MIDI opens and audio starts; its notes kept out of the shared stream; released at quit
  ok: Programmer mode first, LED traffic, the release last
  ok: a real scan found and confirmed the device, saved it, and claimed it mid-session - its notes stop, others' do not, the shared output steps aside
  ok: a second standalone leaves the first one's device alone, and does not hear its pads
````

That is the one command in this plan that may touch a MIDI port at all, and it sets `RP_MIDI_PORT_ALLOW` from its two
ALSA fakes itself.

### Task 4: the shell names no controller, and a contribution is manifest data

Design section 6 and the design's fourth stage, built and reviewed in two halves. The controller leaves the shell and
the backend by mechanism, not by a list: **project sections** (`ProjectSection`, `projectSections`) make the project's
`controller` block the Launchpad package's, parsed by its own hand-written schema and merged by its own rule;
**project services** (`ProjectService`, `projectServices` in `@retroplug/tracker`) move the cart poll, the song timing
and the WRAP/ROM reads into the pack behind a per-store factory; **graph placers** (`GraphPlacer`, `protocol.placer`, a
generated `placers.ts`) make `buildGraph`'s six controller-shaped slots positions a package fills; the **`project` host
group** replaces `controller` and adds `section` / `setSection` / `serviceState`; and **contribution kinds**
(`defineKind`, `KIND_DATA`) make the generator's last two Launchpad hard-codings data. The backend's harness link moves
into the pack (`HarnessSurfaceLink`, `retroplug-launchpad-harness`, `setControllerStaging`), `packages/native` drops the
dependency, and a GENERIC native boundary rule judges it by its own manifest.

The oracle is the graph goldens: `golden/build-graph.json` and `golden/build-graph-roles.json` are byte identical,
because a placer fills the positions the hand-written code filled, and the role-golden runner alone translates the
recorded `model.controller` member to `models.controller` on load. The RED is a slot moved by one position, which fails
twelve controller cases.

Create `packages/core/ts/defineKind.ts`:

````ts
// A contribution kind a package declares for other packages to fill (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section
// 6.5): one package says what an item of the kind IS (its id, the load-time accept that fills its own registry, and its
// own check over the data a contributing manifest carries), and any listed package may contribute items. A kind is
// manifest data, so the generator knows no kind by name.
//
// The two halves of an item live apart on purpose. Its CONTROL-plane half is a value in the contributing package's app
// module, reachable only from the control plane (the app modules carry a role's schema and zod). Its RUNTIME half and
// its data are a manifest entry (`protocol.kinds.<kind>`), which the generated script entry imports and the generated
// protocol module carries as data. The generated registry joins the halves by id, refuses one alone, and hands the
// declaring package its items and their data once at load.
//
// This file is types and an identity function: the declaring package's `control` module default-exports defineKind, and
// the generated registry imports it. Nothing here imports a package above core.
//
// A package that DECLARES a kind owes one more thing: an augmentation of PackageContributions (definePackage.ts) for
// the list its app module carries, the kind's name, so that `definePackage({ <kind>: [...] })` typechecks. Without it
// the generated registry fails tsc at a line that names no manifest; every declaring package's
// ts/packageContributions.ts carries one (see the launchpad's, which also declares the shape of an item).

/** A kind's item, as its declaring package's registry holds it: whatever that package's contract declares, and an `id`
 *  the generated registry reads (the string a project stores, and the one a manifest entry's runtime half is joined
 *  by). */
export interface KindItem {
  readonly id: string;
}

/** The data the contributing manifests declare for a kind's items, by item id: each entry's `data` keys, and nothing
 *  else (the generator refuses an entry key its declaring manifest does not list). */
export type KindData = Readonly<Record<string, Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>>;

/** What a kind's `check` is handed beside the items and their data. */
export interface KindCheckContext {
  /** Every protocol node type the product's graph WIRES (the generated protocol module's PROTOCOL_NODES, which is data
   *  alone): a kind whose data names a node type to set a mode on (a cart's sync node, say) checks it here, because
   *  only the product knows which node types it places. A script node the graph does not wire - one a package's own
   *  placer places, or the routing node the shell builds - is not in the set: nothing could set a mode on it through a
   *  document's node type, so a kind naming one is refused. */
  readonly nodeTypes: readonly string[];
}

/** A contribution kind, as its declaring package states it (a package's `retroplug.kinds.<kind>.control` module). */
export interface ContributionKind<I extends KindItem = KindItem> {
  /** Hand the declaring package its items once, at load, in product order: it fills its own registry (a menu's table, a
   *  default a section reads). Called with every declared kind, an empty list included. */
  accept(items: readonly I[], data: KindData): void;
  /** The declaring package's own checks over the items and their data, run at load before `accept`: what no generic
   *  validation can know (a mode naming a node type no package declares, a field a runtime cannot read). It throws its
   *  refusal, naming the item. */
  check?(items: readonly I[], data: KindData, ctx: KindCheckContext): void;
}

/** The identity function with types: the default export of a declaring package's `control` module. */
export function defineKind<I extends KindItem>(kind: ContributionKind<I>): ContributionKind<I> {
  return kind;
}
````

Create `packages/core/ts/placer.ts`:

````ts
// What a package's graph placer declares (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.3): the slots in the graph
// the shell builds where the package's own nodes go, read by buildGraph at the positions it holds them, in product
// order. A placer is how a package places nodes of its own into a document the shell assembles - the control surface's
// session and its two surface nodes are the launchpad package's - without the shell naming the package, its node types
// or its settings.
//
// The types are core's because buildGraph reads them and a package writes them, and they must import no node code and
// no zod: the generated placers module (packages/retroplug/src/generated/placers.ts) carries one import per declaring
// package, and the planner's bundle is held to carrying no node module and no schema
// (test/script/bundle-protocol.test.ts).
import type { NodeDoc, WireDoc } from "./graphDocument";
import type { KindData } from "./defineKind";

/** Nodes and wires a slot places, in document order: the nodes first in the order given, the wires in theirs. Document
 *  order is plan order on ties (the planner breaks a cycle's tie by it), so a placer says where its nodes sit by which
 *  slot it fills. */
export interface Placed {
  readonly nodes: readonly NodeDoc[];
  readonly wires: readonly WireDoc[];
}

/** A system as a placer sees it: its id, the node type its core is placed as, and the protocol nodes its roles place,
 *  in the system's order. The shell's own system model satisfies it. */
export interface PlaceSystem {
  readonly id: number;
  readonly type: string;
  readonly pipeline: readonly PlaceRole[];
}

/** One protocol role as a placer sees it (the shell's ProtocolRole). */
export interface PlaceRole {
  readonly kind: string;
  readonly node: string;
  readonly config: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
}

/** The protocol node spec a placement's `wires` is handed, as far as a placer may read it: whether the node takes a
 *  controller's launches (the shell's ProtocolNodeSpec carries more, and satisfies this). */
export interface PlaceSpec {
  readonly launches?: true;
}

/** What a placement asks the shell to do, slot by slot. Every member is optional: a placer fills the slots it has
 *  something for, and a slot it leaves out places nothing. */
export interface Placement {
  /** After the host's MIDI input and before the routing node: the session's device input, say. */
  readonly inputs?: Placed;
  /** After the routing node and its wire, before any system's protocol node. */
  readonly session?: Placed;
  /** After the host MIDI out and the wires into it: the session's device output. */
  readonly outputs?: Placed;
  /** The host MIDI out's first inputs, ahead of every system's, so they win a tie at a frame. */
  readonly hostMidi?: readonly { readonly from: string; readonly system: number }[];
  /** Settings merged over a system's protocol node of a type, and over its role's second node: what a session forces on
   *  the cart it drives (a sync mode). A Game Boy's serial-out capture follows them. */
  readonly overrides?: readonly {
    readonly system: number;
    readonly node: string;
    readonly settings: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
  }[];
  /** Wires to add beside a protocol node's own, called after its routing wire and before its writes: where a session's
   *  launches go. `spec` is the node's own spec (PlaceSpec), and `nodeId` is the id buildGraph placed it under, so a
   *  placer names the node it wires into without rebuilding the shell's id convention. */
  wires?(system: number, role: PlaceRole, spec: PlaceSpec, nodeId: string): readonly WireDoc[];
}

/** A package's graph placer: the section / model key it reads (`GraphModel.models[key]`), and where its nodes go. */
export interface GraphPlacer<M = unknown> {
  /** The model key: the project section the placer's model comes from ("controller"). */
  readonly key: string;
  /** The model as the package runs it (a saved app config parsed by the app's own schema). A model read from a
   *  project is normalized by the store's service before it is published, so `DirectGraph`, which takes a model from a
   *  caller, applies this itself - and a model built by hand in a test can apply it too. */
  normalize?(model: M): M;
  place(model: M, ctx: PlaceContext): Placement;
}

/** What a placer may read of the model it is placing into: the systems in slot order, and the manifest data the
 *  packages contribute to the kinds they declare, by kind and then by item id (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md
 *  section 6.5: generated/protocol.ts's KIND_DATA). */
export interface PlaceContext {
  readonly systems: readonly PlaceSystem[];
  /** The data the contributing manifests carry under `kind`, by item id, or an empty record for a kind nothing
   *  contributes to this product. */
  kindData(kind: string): KindData;
}

/** The identity function with types: a placer module's default export, checked against the contract. */
export function definePlacer<M>(placer: GraphPlacer<M>): GraphPlacer<M> {
  return placer;
}
````

````ts
// The project service a package contributes (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.2): the control-plane
// half of a feature whose state outlives a publish - the controller's poll of the cart it drives is the one today. The
// shell builds one INSTANCE per factory per project store, because a plugin host runs one control plane per instance
// (the multi-instance hazard class of the project's memory), so a service's state is its store's and two stores share
// nothing.
//
// The contract lives here rather than in core because its context names TrackerPlayback (this package's), and core
// cannot import a package above it (decision 13). A package contributes the factory from its app module's
// `projectServices` list, which the generated registry concatenates in product order.
import type { RoleInstance } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import type { TrackerPlayback } from "./trackerPlayback";

/** One service instance's view of the store: the section it owns, the systems, and the reads a poll may make. Exactly
 *  every read a poll makes: the systems list and each one's id, ROM path and roles, the battery, the work RAM, a ROM's
 *  header prefix, and the tracker integration's playback hook. */
export interface ProjectServiceContext {
  /** This service's section, as its contributor parses it. */
  section<T = unknown>(): T;
  /** The live systems, in slot order. */
  systems(): readonly {
    readonly id: number;
    readonly romPath: string;
    readonly roles: readonly RoleInstance[];
  }[];
  /** A system's battery, or null when it has none (a real Game Boy, a system that is gone). */
  readSram(id: number): Uint8Array | null;
  /** A system's live work RAM, or null when it cannot be read (an emulated cart has it, a real one does not). */
  readRam(id: number): Uint8Array | null;
  /** The first `bytes` of a file, or null: a ROM's header, which decides how its playback reads the cart's memory. */
  readFilePrefix(path: string, bytes: number): Uint8Array | null;
  /** The playback of the tracker integration these roles name, or null for a system with no tracker. */
  playbackOf(roles: readonly RoleInstance[]): TrackerPlayback | null;
}

/** What a service may do, all of it optional: a service that only publishes a model has no `poll` and no `state`. */
export interface ProjectService {
  /** One poll, on the cadence the UI's song watch calls it at (~30 frames, editor-driven). True = something the graph
   *  reads moved, so the store publishes and notifies. */
  poll?(ctx: ProjectServiceContext): boolean;
  /** The model the graph places for this service's key (`GraphModel.models[key]`), or null for none. Called at every
   *  publish, so it must be cheap enough to run on any edit. */
  graphModel?(ctx: ProjectServiceContext): unknown | null;
  /** What a UI may read of the service, through `host.project.serviceState(key)` (the controller cart's polled
   *  SYNC). */
  state?(ctx: ProjectServiceContext): unknown;
}

/** A package's service contribution: the key its model and its section share, and the instance factory. */
export interface ProjectServiceFactory {
  /** The model / section key ("controller"). */
  readonly key: string;
  create(): ProjectService;
}
````

- [ ] **Step 2: The pack's control plane: its section, its service, its placer, its kind**

The Launchpad's control-plane half lives in `ts/control/`, beside its app module (`index.ts`), whose directory the
device-pack scanner excludes from the portable core: a section that parses a project and a service that polls a cart
are control-plane code, so the scenario's byte-for-byte guarantee holds. `projectSection.ts` is the controller's block
written out by hand (junk snaps per field, an unknown `target` throws naming the value, `merge` is
`ProjectStore.setController`'s body). `projectService.ts` is the store's ~140 lines: the six fields, the poll, the
start-edge anchor, the reader cache and the model, with `{ cartSync, anchor }` as its `state()`. `placer.ts` holds the
two surface node ids, the session node's, `GraphController`, `ControllerSyncRule` (the pack's alone), `NO_SYSTEM`,
`controllerTarget`, `controllerSyncOverride`, `syncModeFor`, `controllerSettings` and the app config `normalize`.
`kind.ts` is the controllerApps kind: `accept` registers every control half in the pack's registry and hands the
manifests' data to the menu's table, and `check` holds ALL of the `syncOverride` validation, with the product's WIRED
node types. `nodeTypes.ts` is the three ids in a module of their own, so the placer imports ids without a node module.
`lgdj-launchpad`'s manifest moves its entry from `protocol.apps` to `protocol.kinds.controllerApps`.

````ts
// The launchpad pack's app module (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md sections 6.1 and 6.2): what it contributes to
// the app itself rather than to a surface. Two things, both the controller's:
//
//   projectSections  the project's `controller` block: the schema it is parsed with, its defaults and how a patch lands
//                    on it. A project that carries a controller block keeps it where it was, and a product without this
//                    pack keeps the block verbatim (no contributor), so nothing is lost either way.
//   projectServices  the control-plane half: the poll of the cart the surface drives, and the model the graph places.
//                    The shell builds one instance per project store, so a DAW's two instances share nothing.
//
// The graph placement itself is `protocol.placer` (ts/control/placer.ts), a module of its own because the planner's
// bundle may carry no node code, and the menus are `retroplug.ui` (ts/ui/index.ts).
//
// This file is the manifest's `retroplug.app` module, and its directory is control plane rather than portable core: the
// device pack's scanner leaves out the directory of an `index` entry, so a sibling of this file (a project section's
// schema, a service's poll, a placer) is never part of the package's MicroQuickJS core, which is what keeps the
// scenario test's byte-for-byte guarantee. A package with its own app module puts its control-plane modules beside its
// index the same way.
import { definePackage } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import type {} from "@retroplug/tracker/packageContributions";
import { controllerSection } from "./projectSection";
import { controllerService } from "./projectService";

export default definePackage({
  projectSections: [controllerSection],
  projectServices: [controllerService],
});
````
