Create `packages/launchpad/ts/control/projectSection.ts`:

````ts
// The controller's project section (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.1): the block a .rplg keeps under
// `settings.controller`, which the Launchpad package owns. The key, its contents and its bytes are the ones the file
// always carried (`controller` stays where it was), so a project that has one loads as it always did and this
// module only says how it is parsed and what a patch does to it.
//
// The parse is written out rather than made of zod fields: the control plane's section contract asks only for a
// `parse`, and this section's schema is small enough to spell (the shapes zod's field builders give it: junk snaps
// to the default instead of failing the whole settings object, which is what keeps a malformed block from resetting the
// project's layout and zoom).
import type { ProjectSection } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import { CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES, type ControllerTarget } from "../enums";
import { defaultControllerApp } from "../registry";

/** The control-surface session a project stores: which app runs, where its launches go and the app's own config. Only
 *  the user's CHOICES live here; the derived song-timing table the predictor needs is built at publish time and never
 *  persisted. */
export interface ControllerSection {
  enabled: boolean;
  /** A controller-app id, e.g. "lsdj-midimap" (the first the product registers is the default). */
  app: string;
  target: ControllerTarget;
  /** 0 = the first system. */
  systemId: number;
  /** The chosen app's OWN knobs (quantise, follow, ...), validated by that app's schema rather than here: the registry
   *  owns their shape, so a new app needs no change to the project's. Small readable JSON, persisted inline like any
   *  other setting. */
  appConfig: Record<string, unknown>;
}

/** The section's key under `settings`, and the model key its placer and service read. */
export const CONTROLLER_SECTION_KEY = "controller";

const isObject = (v: unknown): v is Record<string, unknown> =>
  v !== null && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v);

/** A raw block as an object: a malformed one (null, an array, a number) reads as an empty block and takes the defaults,
 *  rather than failing the whole settings object. */
const blockOf = (raw: unknown): Record<string, unknown> => (isObject(raw) ? raw : {});

/** The block as the session reads it: defaults filled, the target snapped to a launch target this build knows, the
 *  system id a clamped integer. Never throws on junk. */
export function parseControllerSection(raw: unknown): ControllerSection {
  const block = blockOf(raw);
  const target =
    typeof block.target === "string" && (CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES as readonly string[]).includes(block.target)
      ? (block.target as ControllerTarget)
      : "system";
  const systemId =
    typeof block.systemId === "number" && Number.isFinite(block.systemId) ? Math.round(block.systemId) : 0;
  return {
    enabled: typeof block.enabled === "boolean" ? block.enabled : false,
    app: typeof block.app === "string" ? block.app : defaultControllerApp(),
    target,
    systemId: Math.max(0, Math.min(0x7fffffff, systemId)),
    appConfig: { ...blockOf(block.appConfig) },
  };
}

/** A patch merged into the section: a patch naming a different app starts from the patch's own `appConfig`, because the
 *  old app's keys mean nothing to the new one and merging kept them in the .rplg forever; the same app merges one knob
 *  at a time, so a menu row can set one without knowing the others. A `target` that is not a launch target THROWS,
 *  naming the value: the patch would be written into the live settings, the published document and the next save
 *  unread, so a bad value would be a controller that launches nowhere - a package's bug, refused loudly rather than
 *  dropped. */
export function mergeControllerSection(
  current: ControllerSection,
  patch: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>,
): ControllerSection {
  const switching = patch.app !== undefined && patch.app !== current.app;
  const appConfig = switching
    ? { ...blockOf(patch.appConfig) }
    : { ...current.appConfig, ...blockOf(patch.appConfig) };
  const merged = { ...current, ...patch, appConfig };
  if (typeof merged.target !== "string" || !(CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES as readonly string[]).includes(merged.target)) {
    throw new Error(
      `controller target '${String(merged.target)}' is not one of ${CONTROLLER_TARGET_VALUES.join(", ")}`,
    );
  }
  return parseControllerSection(merged);
}

/** The section the generated registry hands the shell: no `version`, because nothing about it has ever needed a
 *  migration, so a project's bytes for a controller are what they always were (an unstamped section is not stamped). */
export const controllerSection: ProjectSection<ControllerSection> = {
  key: CONTROLLER_SECTION_KEY,
  schema: { parse: parseControllerSection },
  defaults: () => parseControllerSection({}),
  merge: mergeControllerSection,
};
````

````ts
// The controller's control-plane half, as a project service (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.2): the
// poll of the cart it drives, the model the graph places for it, and what the menu reads of the poll. Nothing about it
// is the shell's: the contract it implements is @retroplug/tracker/projectService's, and the values it reads come from
// the context that contract gives it.
//
// One INSTANCE per project store: the shell builds one from this factory per store it makes, because a plugin host runs
// one control plane per instance, so a service's state (the song signature, the anchor, the polled SYNC, the edge
// detector, the reader cache) is its store's and two stores share nothing.
import { ROLE_HEADER_LEN } from "@retroplug/core/systemRoles";
import type { ControllerAnchor, PlaybackReader, TrackerPlayback } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerPlayback";
import type {
  ProjectService,
  ProjectServiceContext,
  ProjectServiceFactory,
} from "@retroplug/tracker/projectService";
import { parseAppConfig } from "../registry";
import { type ControllerSection, CONTROLLER_SECTION_KEY } from "./projectSection";
import type { GraphController } from "./placer";

/** One system as the service sees it (the context's own shape). */
type ServiceSystem = ReturnType<ProjectServiceContext["systems"]>[number];

/** What the UI may read of the controller: the cart's SYNC as last polled, and where it was seen starting on its own.
 *  Read through `host.project.serviceState("controller")`. */
export interface ControllerServiceState {
  readonly cartSync: string | null;
  readonly anchor: ControllerAnchor | null;
}

/** One store's controller state and behaviour. See ProjectStore's history for why each field is what it is; the poll's
 *  contract is the shell's song watch (every ~30 frames, editor-driven). */
class ControllerService implements ProjectService {
  /** The live song's signature at the last poll: a change re-publishes the graph, which is how a row edited inside the
   *  cart reaches the grid. */
  private songSig = 0;
  /** The cart's own SYNC setting at the last poll. */
  private sync: string | null = null;
  /** Where the cart last started playback on its own. */
  private anchor: ControllerAnchor | null = null;
  /** The playing edge detector the anchor is sampled on. */
  private wasPlaying = false;
  /** The ROM path the cached reader was built from, and the reader itself. */
  private readerPath = "";
  private reader: PlaybackReader | null = null;

  /** Notice an edit the player made INSIDE the tracker and hand the graph a new model, so a control surface's grid
   *  follows the song. Polled rather than pushed because a cart being edited on its own screen emits nothing. */
  poll(ctx: ProjectServiceContext): boolean {
    const section = ctx.section<ControllerSection>();
    if (!section.enabled) return false;
    const id = this.targetId(ctx, section);
    if (id <= 0) return false;
    // The cart's own playback answers it; a system whose integration has none reads "no sync mode, no signature", which
    // is what the poll did before for anything that was not a tracker cart.
    const sys = ctx.systems().find((s) => s.id === id);
    const playback = sys ? ctx.playbackOf(sys.roles) : null;
    const sram = ctx.readSram(id);
    // One read, two answers. The sync mode is recorded EVERY poll (the player can change it without touching the song),
    // while the re-push is gated on the song actually having moved.
    this.sync = playback?.syncMode(sram) ?? null;
    const anchored = this.sampleAnchor(ctx, sys, playback);
    const sig = playback?.songSignature(sram) ?? 0;
    const songMoved = sig !== this.songSig;
    this.songSig = sig;
    return songMoved || anchored;
  }

  /** The controller as the graph places it, its app config parsed by the app's schema and the derived song-timing table
   *  the predictor runs on, or null with no controller enabled.
   *
   *  The table is built HERE rather than in the node because decoding a battery is a control-plane job - the audio
   *  thread has neither the bytes nor any business running the sav codec. It is rebuilt on every publish and is never
   *  persisted.
   *
   *  KNOWN STALENESS: edits the player makes inside the cart itself publish nothing, so the table lags the cart until
   *  the poll notices the song moved, or something else publishes (docs/launchpad-plan.md risk 5). */
  graphModel(ctx: ProjectServiceContext): GraphController | null {
    const section = ctx.section<ControllerSection>();
    if (!section.enabled) return null;
    const id = this.targetId(ctx, section);
    const sys = ctx.systems().find((s) => s.id === id);
    // The battery is read only when a tracker actually predicts rows from it: a read is an RPC, and a system whose
    // roles run no playback has nothing to say from it.
    const playback = sys ? ctx.playbackOf(sys.roles) : null;
    const sram = playback && id > 0 ? ctx.readSram(id) : null;
    const table = playback ? (playback.rowTicks(sram) ?? null) : null;
    // No readable battery is not a failure: the app still launches rows, it just cannot shade the ones that hold
    // chains. An empty table reads as "no content anywhere".
    return {
      app: section.app,
      target: section.target,
      systemId: section.systemId,
      appConfig: parseAppConfig(section.app, section.appConfig),
      songRowTicks: table ?? [],
      anchor: this.anchor,
      cartSync: this.sync,
    };
  }

  /** The cart's SYNC as last polled, and the start-edge anchor: what the menu's cart-sync row reads. */
  state(): ControllerServiceState {
    return { cartSync: this.sync, anchor: this.anchor };
  }

  /** The system the section names: its own, or the first ("0 is the first system"). */
  private targetId(ctx: ProjectServiceContext, section: ControllerSection): number {
    return section.systemId > 0 ? section.systemId : (ctx.systems()[0]?.id ?? 0);
  }

  /** Watch for the cart starting playback on its OWN - the player pressing START on LSDj's song screen - and capture
   *  where it actually started, so the predictor can be corrected.
   *
   *  Only the not-playing -> playing EDGE, which is what makes this affordable on the structure the graph already
   *  carries: a start is rare and discrete, where streaming the position every block would not be. Returns whether a
   *  new anchor was captured. Emulated carts only - a real Game Boy has no WRAM to read, and dead reckoning stays all
   *  there is. */
  private sampleAnchor(
    ctx: ProjectServiceContext,
    sys: ServiceSystem | undefined,
    playback: TrackerPlayback | null,
  ): boolean {
    if (!sys) return false;
    const reader = this.readerFor(ctx, sys, playback);
    if (!reader || !playback) return false;
    const wram = ctx.readRam(sys.id);
    if (!wram) return false;
    const state = reader.read(wram);
    const playing = playback.anchor.playing(state);
    const started = playing && !this.wasPlaying;
    this.wasPlaying = playing;
    if (!started) return false;
    this.anchor = { rows: playback.anchor.rows(state), seq: (this.anchor?.seq ?? 0) + 1 };
    return true;
  }

  /** The WRAM reader for the cart, built once per ROM. Null for a system whose integration has no playback, an embedded
   *  ROM (nothing to read a header from), or a build its playback has no reader for. */
  private readerFor(
    ctx: ProjectServiceContext,
    sys: ServiceSystem,
    playback: TrackerPlayback | null,
  ): PlaybackReader | null {
    const romPath = sys.romPath ?? "";
    if (!playback || !romPath) return null;
    if (this.readerPath !== romPath) {
      this.readerPath = romPath;
      const header = ctx.readFilePrefix(romPath, ROLE_HEADER_LEN);
      this.reader = header ? playback.anchor.reader(header) : null;
    }
    return this.reader;
  }
}

/** The controller, as a project service the shell builds per store. */
export const controllerService: ProjectServiceFactory = {
  key: CONTROLLER_SECTION_KEY,
  create: () => new ControllerService(),
};
````

````ts
// A control-surface session as the graph places it (docs/modular-graph-phase-b3b-design.md section 4 and
// docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.3): the Launchpad package's placer fills the slots buildGraph holds
// for a package's own nodes, so the shell names no surface node, no session setting and no app. What it places:
//
//   inputs   rp.launchpad.surface-in, right after the host's MIDI input;
//   session  rp.controller.session and its three surface wires, after the routing node;
//   outputs  rp.launchpad.surface-out, after host MIDI out;
//   hostMidi the session's MIDI out first, so it wins a tie at a frame;
//   overrides the sync mode the app needs on the cart it drives (its lsdj-sync node), which a Game Boy's serial-out
//            capture follows;
//   wires    the launches into that cart's sync node.
//
// The sync rule per app is manifest data (a contributing package's `protocol.kinds.controllerApps` entry
// `syncOverride`), so this module names no tracker and no mode: an app declares which node type its launches need, the
// mode that node is put in, and the polled SYNC value that counts as the cart listening. The graph reads it through
// PlaceContext.kindData (generated/protocol.ts's KIND_DATA), and the menu reads the same data from the copy the kind's
// `accept` handed this package (setControllerSyncData): one shape, one reader, two carriers.
import { definePlacer, type Placement, type Placed, type PlaceContext } from "@retroplug/core/placer";
import type { KindData } from "@retroplug/core/defineKind";
import type { ControllerAnchor, RowTicksTable } from "@retroplug/tracker/trackerPlayback";
import { type WireDoc } from "@retroplug/core/graphDocument";
import type { ControllerTarget } from "../enums";
import { CONTROLLER_SESSION_NODE_TYPE, SURFACE_IN_NODE_TYPE, SURFACE_OUT_NODE_TYPE } from "../nodeTypes";
import { parseAppConfig } from "../registry";

/** An app's sync override, as its manifest's `protocol.kinds.controllerApps` entry declares it: which cart sync node
 *  type the app's launches need, the mode that node is put in, and the polled SYNC value that counts as the cart
 *  listening. This package's own type: the kind's data is untyped, so no shell module needs it. */
export interface ControllerSyncRule {
  /** The node type the mode is set on: a system's cart sync node. */
  readonly node: string;
  /** The mode that node is put in. */
  readonly mode: string;
  /** The cart's own SYNC value that counts as listening. When it is polled as anything else the cart is put in `off`
   *  instead; a cart that cannot be read yet is assumed willing. Absent: the mode always. */
  readonly listening?: string;
  /** The mode that means "send this cart nothing", for one polled as not listening. */
  readonly off?: string;
}

/** An enabled controller: the user's choices, and what the control plane derived for it. */
export interface GraphController {
  /** Which controller app runs (by id); an id no app has runs nothing. */
  app: string;
  /** Where its launches go: into the target cart's lsdj-sync node ("system"), or out of the host to a real Game
   *  Boy's Arduinoboy ("midiOut"). */
  target: ControllerTarget;
  /** The system they are for, as the user chose it: 0 is the first system. */
  systemId: number;
  /** The app's own config, already parsed by the app's schema (normalize below, or a publisher's own parse). */
  appConfig: Record<string, unknown>;
  /** The per-row timing table the predictor runs on, derived from the cart's battery. Never persisted: it rides the
   *  document, so a synthesized node is what carries it rather than the `.rplg`. */
  songRowTicks: RowTicksTable;
  /** Where the cart was seen starting on its own, or null on the hardware path / before it ever has. */
  anchor: ControllerAnchor | null;
  /** The cart's OWN SYNC setting, as last polled ("MidiMap", "Lsdj", ...), or null when unreadable. */
  cartSync: string | null;
}

/** The system a controller's host MIDI is tagged with when there is no system to resolve "the first" to: the
 *  kernel's -1, as the unsigned id rp.host.midi-out carries. */
export const NO_SYSTEM = 0xffffffff;

/** The system a controller's launches are for: the chosen one, else the first system, else NO_SYSTEM. An id that
 *  names no live system is left as it is, so its launches go nowhere rather than into whichever cart is first. */
export function controllerTarget(
  controller: Pick<GraphController, "systemId">,
  systems: readonly { id: number }[],
): number {
  if (controller.systemId > 0) return controller.systemId;
  return systems.length > 0 ? systems[0].id : NO_SYSTEM;
}

/** The kind's data, as its `accept` handed this package: the MENU's read of what the graph will do
 *  (controllerSyncOverride below). The graph's own placement reads the same data through PlaceContext.kindData instead,
 *  so a planner that loaded no registry still places the override. Empty until accepted: an app with no rule drives no
 *  cart mode, which is what an app that launches out of the host wants anyway. */
let syncData: KindData = {};

/** Install the kind's data (each item's `syncOverride`, by app id), as the generated registry hands it at load.
 *  Replaces it: a reload's rules are the product's current ones. */
export function setControllerSyncData(data: KindData): void {
  syncData = data;
}

/** An app's rule from a kind's data: the item's `syncOverride`, or null when the app declares none. */
function ruleOfData(data: KindData, app: string): ControllerSyncRule | null {
  const item = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(data, app) ? data[app] : undefined;
  if (item === null || typeof item !== "object") return null;
  const rule = (item as { syncOverride?: unknown }).syncOverride;
  if (rule === null || typeof rule !== "object") return null;
  const { node, mode, listening, off } = rule as ControllerSyncRule;
  if (typeof node !== "string" || node === "" || typeof mode !== "string" || mode === "") return null;
  return { node, mode, listening, off };
}

/** The `lsdj-sync` mode the controller needs the cart it drives to be in, and which system that is.
 *  Null when no controller is driving an emulated cart.
 *
 *  This exists because the two settings MUST agree and nothing made them. `lsdj-sync` defaults to
 *  `midiSync`, while the MI.MAP app's launches are NoteOns that only the `midiMap` translator turns into
 *  row bytes - so enabling a Launchpad on a fresh cart produced a cart being clocked for a mode it was not
 *  in, launches that went nowhere, and LSDj sitting on "WAIT". Reported from a hardware session.
 *
 *  The rule is applied to the document, to the settings of that cart's two sync nodes alone (the node type the rule
 *  names and the decoder reading it), rather than written into the project, which is what makes it safe: nothing
 *  reaches the .rplg, and turning the controller off restores whatever the user had.
 *
 *  `off` when the CART's own SYNC says it is not in MI.MAP. That is not politeness - a cart in LSDJ (master)
 *  mode drives the link itself, so our clock bytes collide with its own and LSDj reports TOO BUSY and stops
 *  rendering properly. Measured in test-native/lsdj-sync-toggle. Better to send a cart that is not listening
 *  nothing at all. */
export function controllerSyncOverride(
  systems: readonly { id: number }[],
  controller: Pick<GraphController, "app" | "target" | "systemId" | "cartSync"> | null | undefined,
): { systemId: number; node: string; mode: string; driving: boolean } | null {
  if (!controller) return null;
  return overrideWith(ruleOfData(syncData, controller.app), systems, controller);
}

/** The app's rule for the graph's placement: the same data, read through PlaceContext.kindData. */
function ruleOf(kindData: PlaceContext["kindData"], app: string): ControllerSyncRule | null {
  return ruleOfData(kindData("controllerApps"), app);
}

/** The override a rule asks for, given the controller and the systems. */
function overrideWith(
  rule: ControllerSyncRule | null,
  systems: readonly { id: number }[],
  controller: Pick<GraphController, "target" | "systemId" | "cartSync">,
): { systemId: number; node: string; mode: string; driving: boolean } | null {
  if (controller.target !== "system" || !rule) return null;
  // "0 is the first system", resolved by the helper the launches are tagged with, so the mode and the launch cannot be
  // aimed at different systems.
  const systemId = controllerTarget(controller, systems);
  if (systemId === NO_SYSTEM) return null;
  const mode = syncModeFor(rule, controller.cartSync);
  // Whether that mode is what makes the app's launches WORK, which is the app's rule and not a mode string a caller
  // may compare against: an app whose "send nothing" mode is spelt differently, or that has none, still reads as not
  // driving.
  return { systemId, node: rule.node, mode, driving: mode === rule.mode };
}

/** The mode a rule asks for, given the cart's own SYNC setting as last polled: the rule's mode unless the cart is
 *  polled as something other than what the app listens for, in which case its `off` (better to send a cart that is not
 *  listening nothing at all than bytes it takes for another master's). */
export function syncModeFor(rule: ControllerSyncRule, cartSync: string | null): string {
  if (cartSync && rule.listening !== undefined && cartSync !== rule.listening) return rule.off ?? rule.mode;
  return rule.mode;
}

/** The session node's settings (@retroplug/launchpad/controllerSession): its system resolved (0 is the node's none),
 *  and the anchor spelt as the node takes it. */
export function controllerSettings(controller: GraphController, target: number): Record<string, unknown> {
  return {
    app: controller.app,
    target: controller.target,
    systemId: target === NO_SYSTEM ? 0 : target,
    appConfig: controller.appConfig,
    songRowTicks: controller.songRowTicks,
    // The node re-anchors when the SEQ changes, so an anchor riding along on later publishes is applied once
    // rather than yanking the playhead back on every unrelated structure edit.
    anchorRows: controller.anchor?.rows ?? [],
    anchorSeq: controller.anchor?.seq ?? 0,
  };
}

/** The controller's placement (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.3). */
export const controllerPlacer = definePlacer<GraphController>({
  key: "controller",
  // The app config as the app's schema parses it (defaults filled, values clamped), the same parse the store runs: a
  // model handed over by anything but a file (DirectGraph's, a test's) is normalized here, so the node and the menu
  // cannot disagree.
  normalize: (model) => ({ ...model, appConfig: parseAppConfig(model.app, model.appConfig) }),
  place(model, ctx): Placement {
    const systems: PlaceContext["systems"] = ctx.systems;
    const target = controllerTarget(model, systems);
    // The app's sync rule as its manifest declares it, through the context's kind data: what the generated protocol
    // module hands every placer, so the planner carries no registry and no app.
    const sync = overrideWith(ruleOf(ctx.kindData, model.app), systems, model);
    // The device's two nodes are placed on their own sides of the session (inputs before it, outputs after), so neither
    // is in a cycle with it; the session's three input wires are its wires, pushed where the session sits.
    const inputs: Placed = { nodes: [{ id: "surface-in", type: SURFACE_IN_NODE_TYPE }], wires: [] };
    const session: Placed = {
      nodes: [{ id: "controller", type: CONTROLLER_SESSION_NODE_TYPE, settings: controllerSettings(model, target) }],
      wires: [
        { from: "surface-in.in", to: "controller.controllerIn" },
        { from: "surface-in.connected", to: "controller.controllerConnected" },
        // How many messages the link lost, so the session repaints what its diff believes was sent (a full send
        // ring, a paint sent while the device was unplugged): the node reports the link's own count, which changes
        // when it does.
        { from: "surface-in.drops", to: "controller.controllerDrops" },
      ],
    };
    const outputs: Placed = {
      nodes: [{ id: "surface-out", type: SURFACE_OUT_NODE_TYPE }],
      wires: [{ from: "controller.controllerOut", to: "surface-out.out" }],
    };
    return {
      inputs,
      session,
      outputs,
      // Driving a cart, it sends no host MIDI; it is wired all the same, as the kernel tagged its MIDI out either way.
      hostMidi: [{ from: "controller.midiOut", system: target }],
      overrides: sync ? [{ system: sync.systemId, node: sync.node, settings: { mode: sync.mode } }] : [],
      wires(system: number, _role, spec, nodeId): readonly WireDoc[] {
        // The launches follow the routed MIDI, as the kernel appended them to its target's inbox: only the system they
        // are aimed at, and only a node type that takes them. The node's own id is the shell's, handed in, so this
        // placer names no id convention.
        if (spec.launches !== true || model.target !== "system" || target !== system) return [];
        return [{ from: "controller.launches", to: `${nodeId}.launches` }];
      },
    };
  },
});

export default controllerPlacer;
````

````ts
// The controllerApps contribution kind's control-plane half (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.5): what
// an app IS to the app's registry, and the checks only this package can make over the data a contributing manifest
// carries.
//
// The kind has two jobs. Its `accept` fills this package's ControllerRegistry from the control-plane halves the
// contributing packages' app modules list, and keeps the manifests' data (each app's `syncOverride`) as the MENU's
// table. Its `check` validates that data before anything is accepted: an override that is not an object, a misspelt
// key, a missing node or mode, an `off` that changes nothing, or a node type no package in this product wires would
// otherwise plan and do nothing.
//
// The data itself stays untyped (KindData): a shell module builds it from the manifests without importing this package,
// which is what lets the planner place an override with no app and no zod in its bundle.
import { defineKind, type KindCheckContext, type KindData } from "@retroplug/core/defineKind";
import { controllerApps, type ControllerAppContribution } from "../registry";
import { setControllerSyncData } from "./placer";

/** The sync override's fields: the node type it applies to, the mode it sets, the polled SYNC value that counts as the
 *  cart listening, and the mode a cart that is not listening is put in. */
const SYNC_KEYS = ["node", "mode", "listening", "off"];

/** One app's `syncOverride`, checked: the data a placer applies and a menu reads. */
function checkSyncOverride(appId: string, sync: unknown, ctx: KindCheckContext): void {
  const where = `the controller app ${appId}'s syncOverride`;
  if (sync === null || typeof sync !== "object" || Array.isArray(sync)) {
    throw new Error(`${where} must be an object, not ${JSON.stringify(sync)}`);
  }
  const rule = sync as Record<string, unknown>;
  for (const key of Object.keys(rule)) {
    if (!SYNC_KEYS.includes(key)) {
      throw new Error(
        `${where} has ${JSON.stringify(key)}, which nothing reads (its keys are ${SYNC_KEYS.join(", ")})`,
      );
    }
  }
  if (typeof rule.node !== "string" || rule.node === "") {
    throw new Error(`${where} needs a "node": the cart sync node type its mode is set on`);
  }
  if (typeof rule.mode !== "string" || rule.mode === "") {
    throw new Error(`${where} needs a "mode": the mode that node is put in`);
  }
  // The node type a mode is set on has to be one this product WIRES: a misspelt one, or one no placer places, would be
  // written onto a node that is not there and do nothing. Only the product knows its wired types, so the generated
  // registry hands them in; the check runs before the `listening` return below, or an override without a listening
  // value would never reach it.
  if (!ctx.nodeTypes.includes(rule.node)) {
    throw new Error(`${where} names ${JSON.stringify(rule.node)}, which no package declares a protocol node for`);
  }
  if (rule.listening === undefined) {
    if (rule.off !== undefined) {
      throw new Error(`${where} names an "off" mode and no "listening" value, so the mode it is for is never used`);
    }
    return;
  }
  if (typeof rule.listening !== "string" || rule.listening === "") {
    throw new Error(
      `${where}'s "listening" must be the polled SYNC value that counts as listening, not ` +
        JSON.stringify(rule.listening),
    );
  }
  if (typeof rule.off !== "string" || rule.off === "") {
    throw new Error(
      `${where} needs an "off": the mode a cart polled at anything but ${JSON.stringify(rule.listening)} is put in`,
    );
  }
  if (rule.off === rule.mode) {
    throw new Error(
      `${where} names ${JSON.stringify(rule.mode)} as both its mode and the mode a cart that is not listening is put ` +
        "in, so the override changes nothing",
    );
  }
}

/** The controllerApps kind: the registry's items, the menu's sync rules, and the checks over the data. */
export const controllerAppsKind = defineKind<ControllerAppContribution>({
  accept(items: readonly ControllerAppContribution[], data: KindData): void {
    for (const item of items) controllerApps.register(item);
    setControllerSyncData(data);
  },
  check(items: readonly ControllerAppContribution[], data: KindData, ctx: KindCheckContext): void {
    for (const item of items) {
      const entry = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(data, item.id) ? data[item.id] : {};
      if (entry.syncOverride !== undefined) checkSyncOverride(item.id, entry.syncOverride, ctx);
    }
  },
});

export default controllerAppsKind;
````

````ts
// The controllerApps contribution kind's control-plane half (ts/control/kind.ts): the checks over a contributing
// manifest's `syncOverride`, and the two things `accept` fills. This is the real kind, not a fixture's copy: the
// generator's suite holds the generic mechanism over a fixture kind, and a package's own data rules are tested by the
// package that owns them (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.5).
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import controllerAppsKind from "../control/kind";
import { controllerSyncOverride } from "../control/placer";
import { controllerApps, type ControllerAppContribution } from "../registry";

// The product's wired node types, as the generated registry hands them: the sync node an override names is a node the
// graph places, so a type no product wires can never be set.
const NODE_TYPES = ["rp.lsdj.sync", "rp.mgb.midi"];

const app = (id: string): ControllerAppContribution => ({
  id,
  label: id,
  config: { parse: (v: unknown) => (v ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown> },
});

/** The check over one app carrying `syncOverride`, with no other data. */
function refuse(syncOverride: unknown): void {
  controllerAppsKind.check!([app("a")], { a: { syncOverride } }, { nodeTypes: NODE_TYPES });
}

test("a syncOverride that is not an object is refused", () => {
  expect(() => refuse(null)).toThrow('the controller app a\'s syncOverride must be an object, not null');
  expect(() => refuse("midiMap")).toThrow('must be an object, not "midiMap"');
  expect(() => refuse([])).toThrow("must be an object, not []");
});

test("a syncOverride key nothing reads is refused, naming the keys there are", () => {
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap", listening: "MidiMap", of: "off" }))
    .toThrow('has "of", which nothing reads (its keys are node, mode, listening, off)');
});

test("a syncOverride with no node or no mode is refused", () => {
  expect(() => refuse({ mode: "midiMap" }))
    .toThrow('needs a "node": the cart sync node type its mode is set on');
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "", mode: "midiMap" })).toThrow('needs a "node"');
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync" })).toThrow('needs a "mode": the mode that node is put in');
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "" })).toThrow('needs a "mode"');
});

test("an off mode with no listening value is refused", () => {
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap", off: "off" }))
    .toThrow('names an "off" mode and no "listening" value, so the mode it is for is never used');
});

test("a listening value and its off mode must both be strings, and off must differ from mode", () => {
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap", listening: 3, off: "off" }))
    .toThrow('"listening" must be the polled SYNC value that counts as listening, not 3');
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap", listening: "" , off: "off" }))
    .toThrow('"listening" must be the polled SYNC value');
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap", listening: "MidiMap" }))
    .toThrow('needs an "off": the mode a cart polled at anything but "MidiMap" is put in');
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap", listening: "MidiMap", off: "" }))
    .toThrow('needs an "off"');
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap", listening: "MidiMap", off: "midiMap" }))
    .toThrow('names "midiMap" as both its mode and the mode a cart that is not listening is put in');
});

test("a node type the product wires no protocol node for is refused", () => {
  expect(() => refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.syncs", mode: "midiMap" }))
    .toThrow('names "rp.lsdj.syncs", which no package declares a protocol node for');
});

test("a well-formed override passes, with or without a listening value", () => {
  // A bare call: the harness has no negated `toThrow`, and a throw here fails the case.
  refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap" });
  refuse({ node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "midiMap", listening: "MidiMap", off: "off" });
});

test("accept fills the app registry and hands the menu the data it applies", () => {
  controllerAppsKind.accept([app("mine"), app("other")], { mine: { syncOverride: { node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "lsdj" } } });
  expect(controllerApps.list().map((a) => a.id)).toEqual(["mine", "other"]);
  expect(controllerApps.get("mine")?.label).toBe("mine");
  // The menu's read: the same data, through the rule the placer applies to a cart.
  expect(controllerSyncOverride([{ id: 1 }], { app: "mine", target: "system", systemId: 1, cartSync: null }))
    .toEqual({ systemId: 1, node: "rp.lsdj.sync", mode: "lsdj", driving: true });
  // An app that declares no rule drives no mode.
  expect(controllerSyncOverride([{ id: 1 }], { app: "other", target: "system", systemId: 1, cartSync: null }))
    .toBe(null);
});
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The shell's project sections and services**

`ProjectSettings` becomes the four core fields plus `sections: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>`; the `controller`
field, `ControllerSettings`, `DEFAULT_CONTROLLER_APP` and the schema's `controller` entry leave `projectConfig.ts`.
The `.rplg` shape is unchanged: `buildConfig` spreads the sections at the top level of `settings` and `parseConfig`
reads them back, so `controller` stays at its key. After the core fields parse, every other key of the raw `settings`
object is a section: through its contributor's migration chain (an unstamped section reads as version 1) then
`schema.parse`, kept verbatim as raw JSON when none contributes it, with a contributor's missing key filled by
`defaults()`. `assertSectionKey` refuses a core key and `__proto__`; `buildConfig` filters core keys out of the
spread; `parseSections` stores each section with `Object.defineProperty`, so a hand-edited `__proto__` key is kept as
DATA. `parseProjectSection` and `serializeProjectSection` are exported with the contributor explicit, so the versioned
half is testable with a synthetic contributor. `ProjectStore` gains `section` / `setSection`, builds one instance per
service factory, replaces `refreshControllerSong` with `pollServices()`, puts each service's `graphModel` into
`GraphModel.models[key]`, and answers `serviceState(key)`. `uiHost.ts` builds the `project` group and loses
`isControllerTarget` and its Launchpad imports; `useSongWatch.ts` calls `pollServices()`.

- [ ] **Step 4: The shell's placers: `buildGraph`'s six slots, and `DirectGraph`'s models**

`buildGraph` walks `model.models` in product order and reads each placer's `inputs` right after `midi-in`, `session`
after the routing node and its wire, `outputs` after host MIDI out and its wires, `hostMidi` at the session point,
`overrides` as each protocol node's settings are made, and `wires` after the routing wire and before the writes; each
Game Boy's capture mode is derived from the override whose node type its pipeline places, which keeps the "capture
follows the forced mode" rule generic. `graph/serialCapture.ts` holds `serialOutCaptureFor` and `SerialOutCaptureMode`
(they read the generic protocol tables), and `graph/controller.ts` is deleted. `DirectGraph.setModel(key, model |
null)` replaces `setController`, applying the placer's `normalize` as the store does, and `DirectGraph` imports
`../generated/packages` for its side effect: a module that reads a kind-filled registry imports the generated
registry, which is the rule the stage 5 review's reproduction made explicit. `engineGraph.ts`'s `PublishedModel`
carries `models`.

Create `packages/retroplug/src/graph/serialCapture.ts`:

````ts
// What a Game Boy captures of its serial out for the mode its cart's sync node runs
// (docs/modular-graph-phase-c2-design.md section 5), which is the shell's rather than a package's: it reads
// PROTOCOL_NODES, the generated table every product carries, so naming a cart's capture table here names no package.
// The controller's placement needs it the same way any
// other override does (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.3), and the placement itself is a package's.
import { PROTOCOL_NODES, type ProtocolNodeSpec, type ProtocolRole } from "./protocolNodes";

/** What a Game Boy captures of its serial out for LSDj's decoder (its node's `serialOutCapture` setting, as the C++
 *  node spells it), which the node gives the core when it takes it, before the core first runs, and at the start of
 *  the first block of a plan that changes it. `listen`: capture the bytes it clocks out itself (LSDj as master sync's
 *  master). `drive`: that, and clock a transfer waiting on an external clock, capturing its bytes too (the
 *  Arduinoboy's part in LSDj MI.OUT). Only MI.OUT may drive: a stopped LSDj master, clocked, takes the idle bytes for
 *  another master's clock and stops answering START (docs/lsdj-master-sync-fix-design.md). `off`: no capture. */
export type SerialOutCaptureMode = "off" | "listen" | "drive";

/** The serial-out capture of a Game Boy whose protocol nodes are `pipeline` (protocolPipeline's), for the mode its
 *  lsdj-sync node runs: `forced`, the controller's override of this system's mode (controllerSyncOverride), when it
 *  has one, else the role's own. Both LSDj-to-host MIDI modes need one: MI.OUT (midiOut) drives, playing the
 *  Arduinoboy that clocks LSDj as the serial slave; master sync (masterSync, SYNC=LSDJ) listens to the clock LSDj
 *  sends as the master. Every other mode is `off`, the forced ones among them (the controller's midiMap and off): the
 *  capture follows the node that decodes it, so a cart the controller drives in MI.MAP is never clocked under the
 *  bytes it is sent. And so is a pipeline that places no lsdj-sync, whatever a role left out of it says: what a
 *  capture delivers is decoded by that role's rp.lsdj.serial-out node, which is not placed, and a driving core would
 *  clock the serial port under the bytes the placed role writes. */
export function serialOutCaptureFor(
  pipeline: readonly ProtocolRole[],
  forced?: string | null,
): SerialOutCaptureMode {
  // The node that declares a capture table is the one whose decoder the pipeline places (LSDj's lsdj-sync), and the
  // table is its package's data: the mapping of a mode to what the core does is the cart's, while this runs in the
  // planner, which may carry no cart at all. A pipeline with no such node captures nothing, whatever a role left out of
  // it says - what a capture delivers is decoded by that role's node, which is not placed.
  const role = pipeline.find((r) => (PROTOCOL_NODES[r.node] as ProtocolNodeSpec).capture !== undefined);
  if (!role) return "off";
  const capture = (PROTOCOL_NODES[role.node] as ProtocolNodeSpec).capture!;
  const mode: unknown = forced ?? (role.config as { mode?: unknown }).mode;
  // An OWN key, not a bare index: the record's prototype would answer "constructor" or "toString" with a function,
  // and a mode is only ever one of the cart's own strings. (hasOwnProperty.call, because the shell's lib target is
  // below Object.hasOwn.)
  return typeof mode === "string" && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(capture, mode) ? capture[mode]! : "off";
}
````

````ts
// Generated by packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs from the desktop product's package list and the
// packages' manifests. Do not edit; edit a manifest and rebuild.
//
// The product's graph placers, in product order: each package's `protocol.placer` module, which says where
// the nodes of a model the shell hands it go (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.3). buildGraph
// reads the slots in this order, so a package's place in `retroplug.products.desktop` is where its nodes land.
// Only the planner imports this module, and it carries types and constants alone: no package's node code and
// no schema.
import type { GraphPlacer } from "@retroplug/core/placer";
import placer_alpha from "@retroplug/alpha/placer";

/** Each package's graph placer, in product order. */
export const PLACERS: readonly { pkg: string; placer: GraphPlacer<any> }[] = [
  { pkg: "alpha", placer: placer_alpha },
];
const placerKeys = new Map<string, string>();
for (const { pkg, placer } of PLACERS) {
  const owner = placerKeys.get(placer.key);
  if (owner !== undefined) {
    throw new Error(owner === pkg
      ? `the package ${pkg} places the graph's model ${placer.key} twice`
      : `two packages place the graph's model ${placer.key}: ${owner} and ${pkg}`);
  }
  placerKeys.set(placer.key, pkg);
}
````

````ts
// A fixture declaring package's control-plane half for a kind that is NOT a real pack's (an `accept` and a `check`), so
// the mechanism is held without naming any real declaring package.
const accepted: { id: string }[] = [];

export function acceptedWidgets(): readonly { id: string }[] {
  return accepted;
}

export default {
  accept: (items: readonly { id: string }[]) => {
    for (const item of items) accepted.push(item);
  },
  check: (items: readonly { id: string }[], data: Readonly<Record<string, Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>>>, ctx: { nodeTypes: readonly string[] }) => {
    for (const item of items) {
      const mode = (data[item.id] ?? {}).mode;
      if (typeof mode !== "string" || !ctx.nodeTypes.includes(mode)) {
        throw new Error(`the widgets item ${item.id} names ${JSON.stringify(mode)}, which no package declares`);
      }
    }
  },
};
````

````ts
// A fixture declaring package's runtime registry: the generated script entry imports this module's `register` and hands
// it the contributing manifests' modules in product order.
const registered: { id: string }[] = [];

export interface WidgetRuntime {
  readonly id: string;
}

export function registerWidgets(items: readonly WidgetRuntime[]): void {
  for (const item of items) registered.push(item);
}

export function registeredWidgets(): readonly WidgetRuntime[] {
  return registered;
````

- [ ] **Step 8: The project's tests: sections, E5, and the migrated shapes**

`test/project/sections.test.ts` is new (13 cases): the defaults a project that never set the section reads; a
hand-edited block's per-field snapping; a settings key no package contributes kept and written back (E5); the
controller block's bytes; `setSection` merging through the contributor and refusing an unknown target; an UNSTAMPED
section reading as version 1 and migrating; a stamped-newer block kept verbatim; and two stores sharing no service
state. The four changed files follow the section: `tolerance.test.ts`'s `futureSetting` is kept (E5, the one existing
test whose meaning changes), `config.test.ts` reads the section and asserts the FILE's top-level `controller`, and
`migrate-string-enums.test.ts`'s expectation is `sections: DEFAULT_SETTINGS.sections`.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/project/sections.test.ts`:

````ts
// The project's sections (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.1): a package owns a block under the .rplg's
// `settings`, and the shell keeps every key it does not own - through a contributor when the product carries one, raw
// when it does not, and never stamped unless the contributor declares a version. The controller is the one section a
// product ships today, so the versioned half of the mechanism is held here through the two functions that implement it.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { MockBackend } from "../../testing/mockBackend";
import { composeAppStores } from "../../src/appStores";
import { lsdjRom } from "../systems/fixtures";
import * as R from "@retroplug/lsdj/codec/regions";
import {
  buildConfig,
  DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
  K_PROJECT,
  parseConfig,
  parseProjectSection,
  projectSection,
  projectSectionOf,
  serializeProjectSection,
} from "../../src/projectConfig";
import type { ProjectSection } from "@retroplug/core/definePackage";
import { type ControllerSection } from "@retroplug/launchpad/projectSection";

/** A section a package could contribute, with the version and one step a real one would carry when it breaks its shape:
 *  v1's `knob` (an integer index) becomes v2's `knob` (a mode name). The step is idempotent-safe, as every step must
 *  be: it runs on a block already in v2's shape without touching it, which is what an unstamped current-shape block
 *  is. */
const VERSIONED: ProjectSection<{ knob: string; size: number }> = {
  key: "versioned",
  version: 2,
  migrations: {
    1: (raw) => ({
      ...raw,
      knob: typeof raw.knob === "string" ? raw.knob : (["a", "b"][Number(raw.knob)] ?? "a"),
    }),
  },
  schema: {
    parse: (raw: unknown) => {
      const block = (raw ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
      return {
        knob: typeof block.knob === "string" ? block.knob : "a",
        size: typeof block.size === "number" ? block.size : 0,
      };
    },
  },
  defaults: () => ({ knob: "a", size: 0 }),
};

// ---- the controller's section, through a project ---------------------------------------------------------------

test("a project that never set the controller reads the contributor's defaults", () => {
  const raw = JSON.stringify({ schemaVersion: K_PROJECT, settings: { layout: "column" }, systems: [] });
  const settings = parseConfig(raw).settings;
  expect(projectSectionOf("controller")?.key).toBe("controller");
  expect(projectSection<ControllerSection>(settings, "controller")).toEqual({
    enabled: false, app: "lsdj-midimap", target: "system", systemId: 0, appConfig: {},
  });
  // And so does a fresh project, without a file at all.
  expect(projectSection(DEFAULT_SETTINGS, "controller")).toEqual(
    projectSection<ControllerSection>(settings, "controller"),
  );
});

test("a hand-edited block is parsed by the contributor, and a patch lands through its merge", () => {
  const raw = JSON.stringify({
    schemaVersion: K_PROJECT,
    settings: { controller: { enabled: "yes", target: "nowhere", systemId: -4, appConfig: { quantise: 3 } } },
    systems: [],
  });
  const settings = parseConfig(raw).settings;
  // Junk snaps to defaults per field, so one bad value cannot reset the project's layout and zoom.
  expect(projectSection<ControllerSection>(settings, "controller")).toEqual({
    enabled: false, app: "lsdj-midimap", target: "system", systemId: 0, appConfig: { quantise: 3 },
  });
});

test("a settings key no package contributes is kept verbatim and written back unchanged (E5)", () => {
  // The shell cannot tell a key a newer build wrote from one of its packages' sections, so it keeps it: stripping it
  // would destroy a downgrade's data on the next save.
  const future = { anything: [1, 2], nested: { deep: true } };
  const cfg = parseConfig(JSON.stringify({
    schemaVersion: K_PROJECT,
    settings: { layout: "grid", futureSection: future },
    systems: [],
  }));
  expect(projectSection(cfg.settings, "futureSection")).toEqual(future);
  const written = buildConfig(cfg.settings, []).settings as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
  expect(written.futureSection).toEqual(future);
});

test("the controller's bytes are what they always were: a saved project round-trips byte for byte", () => {
  // The key, its contents and its order: a section is parsed by its package, and the file is where it stays.
  const withController = {
    ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS,
    sections: {
      ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS.sections,
      controller: { enabled: true, app: "lsdj-midimap", target: "midiOut", systemId: 0, appConfig: { quantise: "beat" } },
    },
  };
  const json = JSON.stringify(buildConfig(withController, []).settings);
  expect(json).toBe(
    JSON.stringify({
      layout: "auto", midiRouting: "sendToAll", audioRouting: "stereo", zoom: 0,
      controller: { enabled: true, app: "lsdj-midimap", target: "midiOut", systemId: 0, appConfig: { quantise: "beat" } },
    }),
  );
  // A second save of the parsed file is the same bytes again (nothing gains a stamp, nothing is reordered).
  const again = parseConfig(JSON.stringify(buildConfig(withController, [])));
  expect(JSON.stringify(buildConfig(again.settings, []).settings)).toBe(json);
});

test("setSection merges through the contributor and refuses what it refuses", () => {
  const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: new MockBackend("/cfg") });
  stores.project.setSection("controller", { enabled: true, appConfig: { quantise: "beat" } });
  stores.project.setSection("controller", { appConfig: { follow: false } });
  expect(projectSection<ControllerSection>(stores.project.settings(), "controller")).toEqual({
    enabled: true, app: "lsdj-midimap", target: "system", systemId: 0,
    appConfig: { quantise: "beat", follow: false },
  });
  // The closed launch-target enum is the package's, so the refusal is too, naming the value.
  expect(() => stores.project.setSection("controller", { target: "nowhere" })).toThrow("controller target 'nowhere'");
});

// ---- the versioned half of the mechanism ----------------------------------------------------------------------

test("a section's own migrations run before its schema, and the root's first", () => {
  // The file's stamp is the OLD one, so the step rewrites what v1 wrote (an index) to what v2 reads (a name).
  expect(parseProjectSection(VERSIONED, { schemaVersion: 1, knob: 1, size: 4 })).toEqual({ knob: "b", size: 4 });
});

test("an unstamped section reads as version 1, so a section that starts unversioned can still migrate", () => {
  // A section is not stamped until it first versions, so the shape before that stamp IS v1: the first versioned
  // release declares 2 and adds one step keyed 1, and every file written before it runs through that step. Reading an
  // unstamped block as current would make that first migration unreachable for every existing project.
  expect(parseProjectSection(VERSIONED, { knob: 1, size: 4 })).toEqual({ knob: "b", size: 4 });
  // A hand-written block already in v2's shape survives the step (it is idempotent-safe), and the schema still fills
  // what neither shape has.
  expect(parseProjectSection(VERSIONED, { knob: "b", size: 2 })).toEqual({ knob: "b", size: 2 });
  expect(parseProjectSection(VERSIONED, {})).toEqual({ knob: "a", size: 0 });
});

test("a key the shell owns, or the prototype's, is not a section a host may read or write", () => {
  // `zoom` is the shell's own settings field, and a package writing it as a section would make the saved file's `zoom`
  // an object the next load resets; `__proto__` would set a prototype rather than store a value. Both are refused with
  // the key named rather than answered with undefined or written into the project.
  const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: new MockBackend() });
  for (const key of ["zoom", "layout", "midiRouting", "audioRouting", "__proto__"]) {
    expect(() => stores.project.section(key)).toThrow(key);
    expect(() => stores.project.setSection(key, { value: 1 })).toThrow(key);
  }
});

test("a core key in a sections record never reaches the file", () => {
  // Defensive: a writer that bypassed setSection still cannot make the shell's `zoom` an object in the .rplg.
  const settings = { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS, sections: { ...DEFAULT_SETTINGS.sections, zoom: 99 } };
  const written = buildConfig(settings, []).settings as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
  expect(written.zoom).toBe(0);
});

test("a hand-edited __proto__ key is kept as data, and never reaches the prototype chain", () => {
  // E5 keeps every key the shell does not own, so a `__proto__` key a hand-edited file carries is data like any other:
  // it must survive the round trip without becoming the settings object's prototype (which would drop it on save).
  // JSON TEXT, not an object literal: `{ __proto__: ... }` in source sets the prototype, while the same text parsed
  // is an own key, which is what a hand-edited file carries.
  const raw = `{"schemaVersion":${K_PROJECT},"settings":{"__proto__":{"polluted":true}},"systems":[]}`;
  const sections = parseConfig(raw).settings.sections as Record<string, unknown>;
  expect(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(sections, "__proto__")).toBe(true);
  expect(sections["__proto__"]).toEqual({ polluted: true });
  expect(({} as Record<string, unknown>).polluted).toBe(undefined);
  const written = buildConfig(parseConfig(raw).settings, []).settings as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
  expect(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(written, "__proto__")).toBe(true);
  expect(written["__proto__"]).toEqual({ polluted: true });
});

test("a section stamped newer than its contributor is kept verbatim, and written back as it came", () => {
  const fromTheFuture = { schemaVersion: 9, knob: { anything: true } };
  // Kept verbatim, not parsed: this build cannot read it, so it must not rewrite it into something it can.
  expect(parseProjectSection(VERSIONED, fromTheFuture)).toBe(fromTheFuture);
  expect(serializeProjectSection(VERSIONED, fromTheFuture)).toBe(fromTheFuture);
  // A section this build does read gets this build's stamp on the way out, and only then.
  expect(serializeProjectSection(VERSIONED, { knob: "a", size: 1 })).toEqual({
    knob: "a", size: 1, schemaVersion: 2,
  });
});

// ---- one service instance per store ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** A full-size LSDj battery with `sync` in the working song's SYNC byte: enough for the byte-level reads. */
function lsdjBattery(sync: number): Uint8Array {
  const b = new Uint8Array(0x20000);
  b[0x813e] = 0x6a; // 'j'
  b[0x813f] = 0x6b; // 'k'
  b[R.kModernRegions.syncMode] = sync;
  return b;
}

test("two project stores share no service state", () => {
  // A plugin host runs one control plane per instance, so a service's polled state is its store's: one store's poll
  // must not answer for another's.
  const be = new MockBackend();
  const a = composeAppStores({ backend: be });
  const b = composeAppStores({ backend: be });
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", lsdjRom());
  for (const stores of [a, b]) {
    stores.project.systems.addSystem("/roms/a.gb");
    stores.project.setSection("controller", { enabled: true });
  }
  // Each store's own system (the backend allocates the ids), and each one's battery.
  const idOf = (stores: ReturnType<typeof composeAppStores>) => stores.project.systems.view()[0].id;
  be.setSram(idOf(a), lsdjBattery(8)); // MidiMap
  be.setSram(idOf(b), lsdjBattery(8));
  const syncOf = (stores: ReturnType<typeof composeAppStores>) =>
    stores.project.serviceState<{ cartSync: string | null }>("controller")?.cartSync ?? null;

  expect(a.project.pollServices()).toBe(true);
  expect(syncOf(a)).toBe("MidiMap");
  // The other store has not polled, so it has nothing of its own to say yet: one instance is not shared.
  expect(syncOf(b)).toBe(null);
  be.setSram(idOf(b), lsdjBattery(9)); // MI.OUT
  expect(b.project.pollServices()).toBe(true);
  expect(syncOf(b)).toBe("MidiOut");
  expect(syncOf(a)).toBe("MidiMap"); // and its own value did not move under it
});

test("a store builds one instance per contributed service, not per publish", () => {
  // The service's state has to survive publishes (a fresh instance per publish would forget the adopted signature and
  // the anchor), which is what polling twice in a row with no edit shows: the second poll is silent.
  const be = new MockBackend();
  const stores = composeAppStores({ backend: be });
  be.seed("/roms/a.gb", lsdjRom());
  stores.project.systems.addSystem("/roms/a.gb");
  stores.project.setSection("controller", { enabled: true });
  be.setSram(stores.project.systems.view()[0].id, lsdjBattery(8));
  expect(stores.project.pollServices()).toBe(true);
  expect(stores.project.pollServices()).toBe(false);
});
````

- [ ] **Step 10: The graph's tests, and the scanner's**

`test/graph/direct-graph.test.ts` is new (the stage 5 review's `norm.ts` reproduction as a case: the registry is
filled by the time `DirectGraph` normalizes a model, so an app's config is the app's parse, not `{}`). The three
changed files move to the model vocabulary (`models.controller`), import `serialOutCaptureFor` from
`graph/serialCapture.ts` and `controllerSyncOverride` from the pack, and load
`setControllerSyncData(KIND_DATA.controllerApps)` for the menu's carrier; every case and its assertions are the
baseline's.

Create `packages/retroplug/test/graph/direct-graph.test.ts`:

````ts
// A model's app config is parsed by the product's own placer, so the registry that placer's app table holds must be
// filled wherever a model can reach one (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 6.5). The fill is a load-time
// side effect of the generated registry, and this module - the publisher that builds systems without stores - is a
// caller that never parses a project, so it imports the generated registry itself rather than trusting whichever of its
// own imports happens to reach a tracker or a kit format first. Without that, `normalize` meets an app the empty table
// does not know and answers `{}`: every knob silently back to the app's defaults.
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { directGraph } from "../../src/graph/directGraph";
import { PLACERS } from "../../src/generated/placers";

test("the model publisher parses a model's app config, so the registry is filled by the time it loads", () => {
  // The publisher is imported for its side effect: it is not called (a DirectGraph needs a native host's RPC).
  expect(typeof directGraph).toBe("function");
  const placer = PLACERS.find((entry) => entry.placer.key === "controller")?.placer;
  expect(placer !== undefined).toBe(true);
  // A user's own value survives; the knobs it does not name fill from the app's schema, which is the table's.
  const normalized = placer!.normalize!({
    app: "lsdj-midimap",
    target: "system",
    systemId: 1,
    appConfig: { quantise: "immediate" },
  }) as { appConfig: Record<string, unknown> };
  expect(normalized.appConfig).toEqual({ quantise: "immediate", follow: true, page: 0 });
});
````

````diff
+async function nodeModules(): Promise<string[]> {
+  const script =
+    'const fs = require("fs"), path = require("path");' +

+  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "-e", script], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
````

- [ ] **Step 13: The backend: the harness link moves into the pack, and the service gains a hook**

`HarnessSurfaceLink.hpp` moves with `git mv` into `packages/launchpad/native/src/launchpad/harness/` (namespace
`rp::launchpad`), in a header-only target of its own, `retroplug-launchpad-harness` (`INTERFACE`, linking
`retroplug-launchpad` for `SurfaceLink.hpp` and `retroplug-node-sdk-headers` for the ring's header), declared BELOW
the pack's device early return so a device build defines none. `EngineRpcService` loses the concrete type and gains
`setControllerStaging(std::function<bool(std::span<const std::uint8_t>)>)`, which `stageControllerIn` and
`renderBlocks` call; an unset hook answers false, as an unset surface did. `main.cpp` and `EngineGraph.test.cpp` build
the harness and bind `queueInput` to it; `retroplug-host` links the harness; `packages/native/CMakeLists.txt`'s link
and `packages/native/package.json`'s `@retroplug/launchpad` are gone. `packages/native`'s `devDependencies` gain
`launchpad`, `n8`, `device-io` and `devtest`, the packs its test binaries reach.

The moves, as one script (each `git mv` stages its move, and `set -e` stops at the first that fails):

````bash
mkdir -p packages/launchpad/native/src/launchpad/harness
set -e
git mv packages/native/src/host/rpc/HarnessSurfaceLink.hpp packages/launchpad/native/src/launchpad/harness/HarnessSurfaceLink.hpp
````

- [ ] **Step 14: The native boundary rule, generic: `packages/native` judged by its own manifest**

`packages/native`'s non-product, non-test targets are judged by `packages/native/package.json` like any package's: a
link or an include of a target of a package it does not declare is refused, and `cmake/packages.cmake` names no pack.
Four things had to be true for the rule: the genex forms `$<TARGET_PROPERTY:t,INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES>` and
`$<TARGET_OBJECTS:t>` are judged by `t`'s owner; the source rule gained the declared-package allowance the link and
include rules already had; three targets are vouched for where they are made (`retroplug-ts-packages[-<product>]`,
`retroplug-box-usb-cdc` with `RP_BOUNDARY_DECLARED n8`, and the plugin's library `retroplug` with
`RP_BOUNDARY_PACKAGES plugin`, with `plugin.cmake` restating the property over it and the formats); and
`RP_BOUNDARY_SKIP` is left for generated code that is nobody's.

````diff
 # and $<TARGET_NAME:x> each name x as it stands in this build, so x is judged; nesting unwraps too

+# judges a link. Anything else ($<TARGET_PROPERTY:...> of another property, a configuration expression) is a value only
+# the build generator knows, which the caller refuses rather than passes unseen.
````

````bash
feat(f5a): the shell names no controller, and a contribution is manifest data

docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md sections 6.1 to 6.7: stage 4, built in two halves. A package owns a block of the
project's settings, a service, a slot in the graph and a contribution kind; the shell and the backend keep none of the
Launchpad. The first half is sections 6.1 to 6.4, the second 6.5 to 6.7, and a fix pass over the first is folded in.

PROJECT SECTIONS. `@retroplug/core/definePackage` gains `ProjectSection` (a key, anything with a `parse`, `defaults()`,
and an optional version, migration chain and `merge`), and `PackageContributions.projectSections`. The generated
packages.ts collects them in product order and refuses a key two packages declare and a key that is one of the shell's
own (layout, midiRouting, audioRouting, zoom). `ProjectSettings` is the four core fields plus `sections`;
`buildConfig` spreads the sections at the top level of `settings` and `parseConfig` reads every non-core key back -
through its contributor's migrations (`migrateRaw`, the root's `K_PROJECT` chain first) and then its schema, kept
verbatim when no package contributes it (E5: a `settings` key no package contributes is kept and written back, which
is what changes test/project/tolerance.test.ts's `futureSetting` expectation, named below). An unstamped section
reads as version 1, the shape before any stamp, so a section that starts unversioned can still migrate: the first
versioned release declares 2 with one step keyed 1 (the user's decision, correcting 6.1). A contributor that declares
a version is stamped with it on the way out, and a section stamped newer than its contributor is kept verbatim and
refused by `setSection` with one warning per key, once. A key that is not a section (one of the shell's own, or
`__proto__`) is refused by `section` and `setSection`, `buildConfig` skips a core key in the sections record, and a
hand-edited `__proto__` key is kept as data through `Object.defineProperty` rather than becoming the settings
object's prototype. The controller's block moves to packages/launchpad/ts/control/projectSection.ts: the same schema
(junk snaps to defaults, the target over the closed enum, the system id clamped, the opaque appConfig), `defaults()`
with the registry's first app, and `merge` as `setController`'s body, an unknown target throwing as it did.

PROJECT SERVICES. `@retroplug/tracker` gains `ProjectService`/`ProjectServiceFactory`/`ProjectServiceContext` beside its
tracker integration contract (decision 13), and an app module declares `projectServices`. ProjectStore builds one
instance per factory per store, `pollServices()` replaces `refreshControllerSong` (the UI's song watch calls it), and a
publish puts each service's `graphModel` into `GraphModel.models[key]`. The controller's ~140 lines (the six fields,
`controllerModel`, the poll, the anchor sampling, the reader cache, `controllerStartAnchor`/`controllerCartSync` as
`state()`) move into the pack's control/projectService.ts; the context offers exactly what they read (its section, the
systems, the battery, the work RAM, a ROM's header prefix and the tracker's playback hook), and its systems come from
store's entries, not the UI view that stats every ROM. The generated PROJECT_SERVICES carries the package beside each
factory, so a duplicate names both.

GRAPH PLACERS. `@retroplug/core/placer` is the contract (Placed, PlaceSystem, PlaceRole, PlaceSpec, PlaceContext,
Placement with inputs / session / outputs / hostMidi / overrides / wires, and GraphPlacer with normalize and place), the
manifest member is `protocol.placer`, and the generator writes src/generated/placers.ts - types and constants only,
the planner's bundle test now holds to carrying no zod, no app and no module that defines a protocol node (read from the
manifests' `protocol.module` and core's defineNode, 22 modules and 64 KB ceilings). buildGraph walks `model.models` in
product order and reads each slot where the controller's code held it; overrides are applied as each protocol node's
settings are made (so a Game Boy's serial-out capture follows them, as before). `Placement.wires` is handed the node's
id, so a placer writes `${nodeId}.launches` and no package copies the shell's id convention. `serialOutCaptureFor` and
mode move to graph/serialCapture.ts (they read the generic protocol tables), and graph/controller.ts is gone: the
surface node types, the session type, `NO_SYSTEM`, `controllerTarget`, `controllerSyncOverride`, `syncModeFor`,
`controllerSettings`, `GraphController` and `ControllerSyncRule` are the pack's. DirectGraph's `setController` becomes
`setModel(key, model | null)`, applying the placer's `normalize` (the app config's parse) as the stores do.

CONTRIBUTION KINDS (6.5). A package's manifest says what a kind IS (`retroplug.kinds.<kind>`: a `control` module
default-exporting `defineKind({ accept, check? })`, a `runtime` { module, register, type }, and the `data` keys a
contributing entry may carry); a contributing package lists its control halves in its app module under `<kind>` and its
runtime halves and data under `protocol.kinds.<kind>`. The generated packages.ts collects each kind's items in product
order, refuses a duplicate id (naming both packages or the one that listed it twice), refuses an item with one half and
not the other, and runs the declaring package's own `check` over the data with the product's node types and then its
`accept`. The generated script entry imports the declaring package's `register` and calls it with the contributing
manifests' modules in product order, keeping the registered-set-equals-manifests check. `CONTROLLER_SYNC` becomes
`generated/protocol.ts`'s `KIND_DATA` (data and types only), buildGraph's adapter goes, and the placer reads
`ctx.kindData`; the Launchpad's `kind.ts` validates each app's `syncOverride` (the shape checks and the node-type
existence check, moved out of the generator) and fills its registry and the MENU's copy of the same data through one
reader. The generator names no Launchpad specifier: its hard-coded `@retroplug/launchpad/registry`, its apps' ids and
`registerControllerApps` call are the kinds table and the declaring package's manifest. src/controller/registry.ts is
deleted; projectConfig's import of the generated module is what fills the pack's table before a project parses.

THE BACKEND'S HARNESS (6.7). HarnessSurfaceLink.hpp moves to the pack
(packages/launchpad/native/src/launchpad/harness/, namespace rp::launchpad), in a header-only INTERFACE target
`retroplug-launchpad-harness`; EngineRpcService loses the concrete type and gains
`setControllerStaging(std::function<bool(std::span<const std::uint8_t>)>)`, which stageControllerIn and renderBlocks
call, and which an unset hook answers false to; retroplug-host and retroplug-engine-graph-test wire the harness's
queueInput into it
and link the new target. packages/native drops `@retroplug/launchpad` and its link. The property is held by the generic
native boundary check now: `native` is judged by its own manifest like any package, so a backend link or include of a
Launchpad target is refused because `packages/native/package.json` does not declare the pack (no pack is named in

rule gained the declared-package allowance its link and include rules had, and native's devDependencies name the packs
its test binaries reach. The plugin's own static library is judged against the plugin's product list instead of native's
manifest, since its link is the product's; a target that states its own reach (the box link's test objects) is judged

WHAT THE SHELL LOSES (6.6). No hand-written file under packages/retroplug/{src,ui,cli} imports @retroplug/launchpad
(the generated modules do, by design), SHELL_IMPORTS loses launchpad/placer and launchpad/registry and gains

held; on stage 3's tree it reports buildGraph's three. The shell keeps both manifest declarations (decision 10), which

THE ORACLE. golden/build-graph.json and golden/build-graph-roles.json are byte-identical (git diff empty). Only the
````

### Task 5: the plugin is its own product, and a bundle is a product's

Design section 7 and the design's fifth stage. The root manifest gains a second product list, `plugin`: the desktop's
packages minus `launchpad` and `lsdj-launchpad`, keeping `n8-wire` before `n8` and `mesen`. The generator takes
`--product`, writes that product's own tree (`build/products/<name>/packages/retroplug/{src,ui}/generated` for a build,
`packages/retroplug/.products/<name>/` for the typecheck) and computes its five hard-coded relative specifiers from the
output directory; an esbuild `onResolve` plugin redirects the shell's relative `../generated/*` imports to the
product's files (the stage opened with the one-file bundle that proved `alias` cannot); the script-node and
render-worker bundles become product-supplied sources compiled once per distinct list content, with an OBJECT library
per set; `retroplug_product(<product> LIST <name>)` exists and refuses an unlisted `PACKAGES`; the plugin's formats pass
`LIST plugin`; and `plugin.cmake`'s assertions invert. Then E3, the docs pass and the design's as-built section.

The plugin as a result: no Launchpad module in any of its four bundles, no controller placement or sync override (E2),
its `rp.lsdj.serial-out` at span label 22 (E6), and a fresh project with no `controller` block (E8).

- [ ] **Step 2: The generator: `--product`, the product's tree, and the two scripts beside it**

`generate({ root, product, buildDir, productsDir })` validates a list as the desktop's is validated (names, no
duplicate, no shell), and a non-desktop list must be a SUBSEQUENCE of the desktop's in relative order, so the
registration order and the set of packages the configure adds cannot disagree; `order()` skips the shell's "a
contributing dependency the shell declares" rule for a NON-desktop list only (a plugin list may drop a contributing
package deliberately), and the desktop keeps the old refusal. Span labels are positional for every non-desktop list
(`ScriptHost::spanLabelFor` numbers what it is handed) while the desktop keeps the strict no-gap rule. The five
specifiers the output hard-coded relative to the shell's tree are computed from the output directory, every generated
header names the product it was written for, and `--products-dir` gives the typecheck its own tree outside `build/`.
`packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/product-lists.mjs` reports the manifest's lists, because CMake cannot enumerate a JSON
object's keys; `scripts/typecheck-products.mjs` runs one `tsc -p` per non-desktop list the manifest names, resolving
the compiler as `pnpm typecheck` always has. `packages/retroplug/package.json`'s typecheck is the generator plus that
script, on one program; `.gitignore` names `.products/` with its reason.

Create `packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/product-lists.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Prints the root manifest's product lists, one per line, as `<name>=<package>,<package>,...` for the configure
// (CMakeLists.txt reads retroplug.products into RP_PRODUCT_PACKAGES_<name>): CMake's JSON reader takes a member by name
// and cannot enumerate an object's keys, so the enumeration is here, beside the generator that reads the same lists.
//
//   node packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/product-lists.mjs <root package.json>
//
// A list's own shape (names, no duplicate, no shell) is validated by the generator, which reads the same JSON; this
// script only reports, and refuses a manifest with no products at all.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

const manifestPath = process.argv[2];
if (!manifestPath) {
  console.error("usage: node packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/product-lists.mjs <root package.json>");
  process.exit(2);
}
const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifestPath, "utf8"));
const products = manifest.retroplug?.products;
const names = Object.keys(products ?? {});
if (names.length === 0) {
  console.error(`${manifestPath} has no retroplug.products lists`);
  process.exit(1);
}
for (const name of names) {
  const list = products[name];
  if (!Array.isArray(list) || list.some((entry) => typeof entry !== "string")) {
    console.error(`${manifestPath}: retroplug.products.${name} is not a list of package names`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
  // Comma-separated: CMake lists are semicolon-separated, and a line is read as one list element before it is split.
  console.log(`${name}=${list.join(",")}`);
}
````

Create `packages/retroplug/scripts/typecheck-products.mjs`:

````js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Type-checks every non-desktop product's generated tree (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md sections 7.2 and 11,
// item 5): for each list the root package.json's retroplug.products declares but the desktop's, the generator writes
// the product's modules, and its own tsconfig program checks them against the shell's real sources.
//
// The tree goes under the shell's `.products/` (gitignored), NOT under build/: build.sh and build.bat configure when
// `build/CMakeCache.txt` is missing, and a typecheck before a build must not leave a directory a later build reads as
// a configured tree. A build's own product trees still land under its binary directory, where its bundle targets
// expect them.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { generate } from "./lib/packages.mjs";

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const SHELL = resolve(HERE, "..");
const ROOT = resolve(SHELL, "..", "..");
const PRODUCTS = join(SHELL, ".products");
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
// The compiler `pnpm typecheck` runs: the workspace's `tsc` is the root's `typescript-5` (an alias of 5.7.3), not a
// package's own `typescript` dependency, so the same binary is run here rather than resolved from the shell's.
const tsc = require.resolve("typescript-5/bin/tsc");

const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(ROOT, "package.json"), "utf8"));
const lists = Object.keys(manifest.retroplug?.products ?? {});
let failed = false;
for (const product of lists) {
  // The desktop's tree is the shell's own, which the program this script runs beside (`tsc --noEmit`) already covers.
  if (product === "desktop") continue;
  generate({ root: ROOT, product, productsDir: PRODUCTS });
  const program = join(PRODUCTS, product, "tsconfig.json");
  console.log(`typecheck: the ${product} product's tree (${program})`);
  const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [tsc, "-p", program, "--noEmit"], { stdio: "inherit" });
  if (result.status !== 0) failed = true;
}
process.exit(failed ? 1 : 0);
````

````diff
+ *  publishes there. */
+function workspacePathEntries(root, fromDir) {

+    const manifestPath = join(dir, name, "package.json");
````
