- [ ] **Step 4: The CMake: the product lists, the bundle sets, and the product-supplied bundles**

`CMakeLists.txt` reads every member of `retroplug.products` into `RP_PRODUCT_PACKAGES_<name>` (through the script
above) and keeps `RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES`; `retroplug_check_product_lists()` refuses a list that is not the desktop's
subsequence (by name, a duplicate included) and runs at the root configure. `retroplug_bundles(<set>)` makes the
generator target and the four bundle targets once per DISTINCT list content (the desktop's keep their names, paths and
bytes; the plugin's take a `-plugin` suffix and write under `build/products/plugin/native/`), with per-product
byproducts and one OBJECT library per set, in the new `packages/native/cmake/product-bundles.cmake`, included before
the first product. `retroplug_product` takes exactly one of `LIST` and `PACKAGES` and REFUSES a non-DEVICE product
whose `PACKAGES` equal no list. The script-node and render-worker bundles leave `retroplug-backend` (it declares them
extern and supplies neither) and become sources each product's targets carry. `plugin.cmake`'s assertions invert, the
CLI bundle, SDK assets and example sessions get their dependency on the desktop's generator back, the stale
backend-to-render-worker edge goes, and `warnings.cmake` puts a bundle set's object library in the `/W4 /WX` list
through a global property.

Create `packages/native/cmake/product-bundles.cmake`:

````cmake
# Included by packages/native/CMakeLists.txt before the first retroplug_product(), which every product's targets then
# get two of the four embedded bundles from (the script nodes and the render worker): the backend declares those two
# symbols extern, so a product that does not supply them fails to link, and a product's script host loads ITS node set.
# The control plane and the UI are embedded by the product's own sources, through the variables this file sets.
#
# The desktop's four bundles are the shell's own tree's, written under the binary directory's native/, the paths every
# existing reference reads; every other list has its own set, under build/products/<name>/, built from the tree the
# generator writes for that list
# (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 7.2). A product's packages are one of the root manifest's lists:
# retroplug_product() refuses packages that are no list's, since a bundle set is built from a list's tree.

# The generator and the shell it lives in. The shell is not a product package, so its manifest is named beside the
# product's; both are derived from the generator's path rather than from a name either side has to agree on.
set(RP_TS_GENERATOR "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs")
get_filename_component(RP_TS_SHELL "${RP_TS_GENERATOR}/../../.." ABSOLUTE)

# --- the per-product generated modules and embedded bundles (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 7.2).
#
# Every product has four embedded bundles: the control plane, the React UI, the script nodes and the render worker.
# The desktop's are the shell's own tree's (src/generated, ui/generated), which the shell program, the pure tier and
# every existing path already read, and its bundles keep the names and paths they had. Any other product's are written
# under build/products/<name>/, laid out as the shell's tree is, by the same generator run with --product: its package
# list differs, so its registries do (the plugin's carry no Launchpad); its bundles are built from that tree through
# tools/product-generated.js, the esbuild resolver that points the shell's `../generated/packages`-style imports at the
# product's file. The bundle targets are made ONCE PER DISTINCT LIST CONTENT: two products whose lists are equal share
# one set of bundles, named after the first of them.
#
# retroplug_bundles(<name>) defines that product's four bundle targets (once) and hands the caller the C arrays' paths,
# the targets and the generator target in RP_BUNDLE_<name>_*. retroplug_product() adds the script-node and render-worker
# arrays to its TARGETS: the backend declares those two symbols extern, so every product has to supply them, and a
# product's script host then loads ITS nodes. The control plane and the UI are embedded by the product's own sources
# (the plugin through PluginDSP.cpp/PluginUI.cpp, the SDL binary and the UI test through their own lists), which is why
# they are variables here rather than target sources.
function(retroplug_bundles name)
    # The list's CONTENT decides which set a product shares: two products whose packages are equal build one set of
    # bundles, named after the first of them that asked for it.
    get_property(_packages GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLE_PACKAGES_${name})
    set(_key "${name}")
    string(REPLACE ";" "-" _content "${_packages}")
    if(_content)
        get_property(_shares GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLE_SHARED_${_content})
        if(_shares)
            set(_key "${_shares}")
        else()
            set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLE_SHARED_${_content} "${name}")
        endif()
    endif()
    get_property(_done GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLES_${_key}_DONE)
    if(NOT _done)
        get_property(_packages GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLE_PACKAGES_${_key})
        if(_key STREQUAL "desktop")
            set(_suffix "")
            set(_dir "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/native")
            set(_product_tree "")
            set(_generated "${RP_TS_SHELL}/src/generated")
            set(_ui_generated "${RP_TS_SHELL}/ui/generated")
            set(_cli_generated "${RP_TS_SHELL}/cli/generated")
            set(_tsconfigs "${RP_TS_SHELL}/tsconfig.host-modules.json" "${RP_TS_SHELL}/tsconfig.paths.json")
            set(_generator_args "")
            set(_manifests "${RP_TS_SHELL}/package.json")
            foreach(_package IN LISTS _packages)
                list(APPEND _manifests "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/${_package}/package.json")
            endforeach()
        else()
            set(_suffix "-${_key}")
            set(_dir "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/products/${_key}/native")
            set(_product_tree "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/products/${_key}/packages/retroplug")
            set(_generated "${_product_tree}/src/generated")
            set(_ui_generated "${_product_tree}/ui/generated")
            set(_cli_generated "")
            set(_tsconfigs "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/products/${_key}/tsconfig.json"
                           "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/products/${_key}/tsconfig.paths.json")
            set(_generator_args --product ${_key} --build-dir ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})
            set(_manifests "${RP_TS_SHELL}/package.json" "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/package.json")
            foreach(_package IN LISTS _packages)
                list(APPEND _manifests "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/${_package}/package.json")
            endforeach()
        endif()
        # The scripts' one product form, emitted only for a set that has a tree of its own (the desktop's is the
        # shell's).
        set(_product_args "")
        if(_product_tree)
            set(_product_args --product-dir "${_product_tree}")
        endif()
        set(_generated_files "${_generated}/packages.ts" "${_generated}/consoles.ts" "${_generated}/protocol.ts"
                             "${_generated}/scriptNodes.ts" "${_generated}/placers.ts"
                             "${_ui_generated}/menus.ts" "${_ui_generated}/views.ts")
        if(_cli_generated)
            list(APPEND _generated_files "${_cli_generated}/tools.ts")
        endif()
        set(_generator_target "retroplug-ts-packages${_suffix}")
        add_custom_target(${_generator_target}
            COMMAND ${NODE_EXECUTABLE} ${RP_TS_GENERATOR} ${_generator_args}
            BYPRODUCTS ${_generated_files} ${_tsconfigs}
            SOURCES ${RP_TS_GENERATOR} ${_manifests} "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/package.json"
                    "${RP_TS_SHELL}/host-modules.json" "${RP_TS_SHELL}/tsconfig.aliases.json"
            COMMENT "Generating the TS package registries${_suffix} and the typecheck paths"
            VERBATIM)
        # The generator IS the shell's script (the shell's tree holds it, and it writes registries), so this target
        # names the shell by construction and is nobody's to judge against the native package's declarations: the
        # boundary check's voucher, stated here where that is read (cmake/packages.cmake).
        set_target_properties(${_generator_target} PROPERTIES RP_BOUNDARY_SKIP "the shell's own TS generator")

        # --- control-plane bundle: pluginControlPlane.ts -> bytecode C array (mirrors ui-regenerate). The DPF plugin
        # evals this at construct to compose the stores (what runs on the audio thread is the script nodes, below).
        set(_cp_js "${_dir}/cp-bundle.js")
        set(_cp_c "${_dir}/cp-bundle_data.c")
        set_source_files_properties(${_cp_c} PROPERTIES GENERATED TRUE)
        add_custom_target(retroplug-cp-bundle${_suffix} ALL
            BYPRODUCTS ${_cp_js} ${_cp_c} ${_cp_c}.new
            COMMAND ${NODE_EXECUTABLE} ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/build-controlplane.js ${_cp_js} ${_product_args}
            COMMAND ${_TJSC_COMMAND} -m -s -p rp_ -o ${_cp_c}.new ${_cp_js}
            COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different ${_cp_c}.new ${_cp_c}
            COMMENT "Regenerating control-plane bundle${_suffix} (esbuild + bytecode)"
            VERBATIM)
        if(TARGET ${_TJSC_DEP})
            add_dependencies(retroplug-cp-bundle${_suffix} ${_TJSC_DEP})
        endif()
        add_dependencies(retroplug-cp-bundle${_suffix} ${_generator_target})

        # --- the UI bundle: main.tsx -> bytecode C array (React entry via build-ui.js).
        set(_ui_js "${_dir}/ui-bundle.js")
        set(_ui_c "${_dir}/ui-bundle_data.c")
        set_source_files_properties(${_ui_c} PROPERTIES GENERATED TRUE)
        add_custom_target(retroplug-ui-bundle${_suffix}
            BYPRODUCTS ${_ui_js} ${_ui_c} ${_ui_c}.new ${_ui_js}.d
            COMMAND ${NODE_EXECUTABLE} ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/build-ui.js
                    ${_ui_js} ${_ui_js}.d
                    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/retroplug/ui/main.tsx ${_product_args}
            COMMAND ${_TJSC_COMMAND} -m -s -p rp_ -o ${_ui_c}.new ${_ui_js}
            COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different ${_ui_c}.new ${_ui_c}
            COMMENT "Regenerating UI bundle${_suffix} (esbuild + bytecode)"
            VERBATIM)
        if(TARGET ${_TJSC_DEP})
            add_dependencies(retroplug-ui-bundle${_suffix} ${_TJSC_DEP})
        endif()
        add_dependencies(retroplug-ui-bundle${_suffix} ${_generator_target})

        # --- the script-node bundle: the product's generated scriptNodes.ts, every TS node type its packages
        # contribute, esbuilt to a global-code IIFE (each Engine's script host evaluates it on two BARE QuickJS
        # runtimes, which have no module loader) + tjsc'd WITHOUT -m to global-code bytecode, as the render worker is.
        # The array name derives from the output stem: rp_script_bundle[] + _size, the same for every product (the
        # backend declares them extern).
        set(_script_js "${_dir}/script-bundle.js")
        set(_script_c "${_dir}/script-bundle_data.c")
        set_source_files_properties(${_script_c} PROPERTIES GENERATED TRUE)
        add_custom_target(retroplug-script-bundle${_suffix}
            BYPRODUCTS ${_script_js} ${_script_c} ${_script_c}.new
            COMMAND ${NODE_EXECUTABLE} ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/build-session.js
                    ${_generated}/scriptNodes.ts ${_script_js} iife ${_product_args}
            COMMAND ${_TJSC_COMMAND} -s -p rp_ -o ${_script_c}.new ${_script_js}
            COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different ${_script_c}.new ${_script_c}
            COMMENT "Bundling the script nodes${_suffix} (esbuild iife + global-code bytecode)"
            VERBATIM)
        if(TARGET ${_TJSC_DEP})
            add_dependencies(retroplug-script-bundle${_suffix} ${_TJSC_DEP})
        endif()
        add_dependencies(retroplug-script-bundle${_suffix} ${_generator_target})

        # --- the render-worker bundle: src/render/worker.ts, the same sources for every product (it renders the plan it
        # is handed), built against the product's registries through its generated tree.
        set(_render_js "${_dir}/render-worker-bundle.js")
        set(_render_c "${_dir}/render-worker-bundle_data.c")
        set_source_files_properties(${_render_c} PROPERTIES GENERATED TRUE)
        add_custom_target(retroplug-render-worker-bundle${_suffix}
            BYPRODUCTS ${_render_js} ${_render_c} ${_render_c}.new
            COMMAND ${NODE_EXECUTABLE} ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/tools/build-session.js
                    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/packages/retroplug/src/render/worker.ts ${_render_js} iife ${_product_args}
            COMMAND ${_TJSC_COMMAND} -s -p rp_ -o ${_render_c}.new ${_render_js}
            COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy_if_different ${_render_c}.new ${_render_c}
            COMMENT "Bundling render worker${_suffix} (esbuild iife + global-code bytecode)"
            VERBATIM)
        if(TARGET ${_TJSC_DEP})
            add_dependencies(retroplug-render-worker-bundle${_suffix} ${_TJSC_DEP})
        endif()
        add_dependencies(retroplug-render-worker-bundle${_suffix} ${_generator_target})

        # The two arrays, compiled ONCE per set: every product target of a set uses these objects, where before each
        # one compiled its own copy (the render worker's array is 4.7 MB of C, and eight desktop products, each test
        # binary and four plugin formats compiled it). An object library keeps one definition per binary and one
        # compile per set; retroplug_product() adds its objects to each of its TARGETS.
        add_library(retroplug-bundles${_suffix}-objects OBJECT EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL ${_script_c} ${_render_c})
        add_dependencies(retroplug-bundles${_suffix}-objects
                         retroplug-script-bundle${_suffix} retroplug-render-worker-bundle${_suffix})
        # Judged at our own warning level, as the products that compiled the arrays were (cmake/warnings.cmake reads
        # this property: a set's name is the list's, so naming them here would miss the next one).
        set_property(GLOBAL APPEND PROPERTY RP_BUNDLE_OBJECTS_TARGETS "retroplug-bundles${_suffix}-objects")

        set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLES_${_key}_SUFFIX "${_suffix}")
        set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLES_${_key}_DIR "${_dir}")
        set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLES_${_key}_DONE TRUE)
    endif()
    # The caller's view, whether this product's set is its own or one it shares.
    get_property(_suffix GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLES_${_key}_SUFFIX)
    get_property(_dir GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLES_${_key}_DIR)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_KEY "${_key}" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_GENERATOR "retroplug-ts-packages${_suffix}" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_CP_TARGET "retroplug-cp-bundle${_suffix}" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_UI_TARGET "retroplug-ui-bundle${_suffix}" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_SCRIPT_TARGET "retroplug-script-bundle${_suffix}" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_RENDER_TARGET "retroplug-render-worker-bundle${_suffix}" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_CP_C "${_dir}/cp-bundle_data.c" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_UI_C "${_dir}/ui-bundle_data.c" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_SCRIPT_C "${_dir}/script-bundle_data.c" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_RENDER_C "${_dir}/render-worker-bundle_data.c" PARENT_SCOPE)
    set(RP_BUNDLE_${name}_OBJECTS "retroplug-bundles${_suffix}-objects" PARENT_SCOPE)
endfunction()


# The desktop's set, made here so every product declared below can share it and every existing reference to its C arrays
# (CP_BUNDLE_C, UI_BUNDLE_C) keeps its meaning. A product declared with LIST <name> gets its own set through
# retroplug_product().
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_BUNDLE_PACKAGES_desktop "${RP_PRODUCT_PACKAGES_desktop}")
retroplug_bundles(desktop)
set(CP_BUNDLE_C "${RP_BUNDLE_desktop_CP_C}")
set(UI_BUNDLE_C "${RP_BUNDLE_desktop_UI_C}")
````

Create `packages/native/test/packages/product-lists/CMakeLists.txt`:

````cmake
# retroplug_product()'s list rules and the subsequence rule the root configure applies, configured as a child project
# by packages/native/cmake/tests.cmake. Each is a refusal of the DECLARATION, so the fixture needs no package and no
# engine: one INTERFACE target for the product to attach to, and the list globals the root configure fills from the
# manifest. PRODUCT_LIST_CASE picks the shape:
#
#   list-both        LIST and PACKAGES together: refused, they are one choice
#   list-unknown     LIST naming a list the manifest does not declare: refused, naming it
#   packages-no-list PACKAGES naming packages that are no list's, in a build that makes bundles: refused, since the
#                    product's four bundles are built from a list's generated tree
#   subsequence-out-of-order  a list that reverses the desktop's order: refused by retroplug_check_product_lists()
#   subsequence-twice        a list naming a package twice: refused as a duplicate, not as "out of order"
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.19)
project(retroplug_product_lists NONE)

if(NOT RP_ROOT)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/product-lists/CMakeLists.txt: pass -DRP_ROOT=<the repository root>")
endif()
if(NOT PRODUCT_LIST_CASE)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/product-lists/CMakeLists.txt: pass -DPRODUCT_LIST_CASE=<case>")
endif()

include("${RP_ROOT}/cmake/packages.cmake")

# The root configure's globals, as it reads them from the root manifest: a list is only judged against the desktop's.
set(RP_DESKTOP_PACKAGES "alpha;beta")
set(RP_PRODUCT_PACKAGES_desktop "alpha;beta")
set(RP_PRODUCT_PACKAGES_out-of-order "beta;alpha")
set(RP_PRODUCT_PACKAGES_twice "alpha;alpha")
# One list at a time, so the case under test is the one the rule reaches first (the rule walks the names in order).
if(PRODUCT_LIST_CASE STREQUAL "subsequence-twice")
    set(RP_PRODUCT_LIST_NAMES "desktop;twice")
else()
    set(RP_PRODUCT_LIST_NAMES "desktop;out-of-order")
endif()
# A package the product path finds, so `packages-no-list` reaches the bundle rule rather than the package guard: the
# real configure's table is retroplug_package()'s, which this fixture does not call.
set_property(GLOBAL PROPERTY RP_PACKAGES alpha)

# The bundle machinery, which the refusal of a PACKAGES product with no list needs to know the build makes bundles: the
# refusal is retroplug_product()'s and fires before this is called, so a case that reaches the stub has not refused.
function(retroplug_bundles name)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/product-lists: retroplug_product() accepted ${name}, whose packages are no list")
endfunction()

if(PRODUCT_LIST_CASE STREQUAL "packages-no-list")
    # The product path runs to the bundle rule, so it needs a target it can add sources and include directories to.
    enable_language(CXX)
    add_library(rp_fixture_product STATIC fixture.cpp)
else()
    # Every other case is refused before the product touches a target.
    add_library(rp_fixture_product INTERFACE)
endif()

if(PRODUCT_LIST_CASE STREQUAL "list-both")
    retroplug_product(rp_fixture_product LIST desktop PACKAGES alpha)
elseif(PRODUCT_LIST_CASE STREQUAL "list-unknown")
    retroplug_product(rp_fixture_product LIST nowhere)
elseif(PRODUCT_LIST_CASE STREQUAL "packages-no-list")
    retroplug_product(rp_fixture_product PACKAGES alpha)
elseif(PRODUCT_LIST_CASE STREQUAL "subsequence-out-of-order")
    retroplug_check_product_lists()
elseif(PRODUCT_LIST_CASE STREQUAL "subsequence-twice")
    retroplug_check_product_lists()
else()
    message(FATAL_ERROR "test/packages/product-lists: no case ${PRODUCT_LIST_CASE}")
endif()
message(STATUS "product-lists/${PRODUCT_LIST_CASE} holds")
````

`build.sh` and `build.bat` configured when `build/` did not EXIST, and the typecheck's product tree was written under
`build/`, so CI's own order (typecheck, then `./build.sh`) skipped the configure and failed on `could not load cache`
(the stage 5 review's Critical). Both scripts now test `build/CMakeCache.txt` (the batch file's `BUILD_EXISTED` became
`CONFIGURED`), and the typecheck writes `packages/retroplug/.products/` instead. The RED, on a scratch extract of the
tip before the fix: the old typecheck left `build/products/` and no cache, and `./build.sh` under a logging `cmake`
shim printed the build call alone:


````text

==> Building (-j32)
````

/tmp/f5apro/fresh5/build`).

- [ ] **Step 7: The tools: one `onResolve` redirect, one form of `--product-dir`**

`tools/product-generated.js` matches imports of `.../generated/(packages|consoles|protocol|scriptNodes|placers|
menus|views)` whose importer is under the shell's `src/` or `ui/` (never an entry point) and answers with the
product's file. It is taken by `build-controlplane.js` (`OUT.js [--product-dir <dir>]`), `build-ui.js` (`<bundle.js>
[bundle.d] [ui-entry.tsx] [--product-dir <dir>]`, so `bundleInputs` serves the checks) and `build-session.js`
(`--product-dir <dir>`): one form in all three, refused when bare, emitted by CMake only for a set that has a product
tree. A product's tree is outside the shell, so its builds also hand the shell's `node_modules` to esbuild as
`nodePaths`, and `bundleInputs` is async in both scripts (esbuild refuses plugins in `buildSync`).

Create `tools/product-generated.js`:

````js
// esbuild's `onResolve` half of the per-product bundles (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 7.2): a
// product whose package list differs from the desktop's has its own generated modules, written under the build
// directory in the shape the shell's tree has, and this plugin makes the shell's own sources read them.
//
// The shell's sources import their generated modules by RELATIVE path ("../generated/packages", "./generated/menus"),
// and esbuild's `alias` only substitutes package specifiers: a one-file bundle with an alias for `generated` still
// compiled the desktop's file (a relative import is resolved against its importer, never through the alias table). So
// the redirect is a resolver: an import whose path ends in one of the generated modules' names, from an importer under
// the shell's src/ or ui/, is answered with the product's file. The entry points are never redirected (a script-node
// bundle's entry IS the product's generated module), and neither is an import from anywhere else: a product's own tree
// already names its siblings, and a package's module names no generated file.
//
//   const { productGenerated } = require("./product-generated");
//   esbuild.build({ ..., plugins: [productGenerated({ dir: "<build>/products/<name>/packages/retroplug" })] })
//
// No plugin (no `dir`) is the desktop: the shell's tree holds the desktop's modules, so nothing is redirected and the
// build takes esbuild's synchronous path (a plugin needs the asynchronous one).
const path = require("path");

const REPO_ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, "..");
const SHELL = path.join(REPO_ROOT, "packages/retroplug");

/** The generated modules and the tree they live in: the protocol tables and the app registry are src/, the UI's two
 *  are ui/. */
const GENERATED = {
  packages: "src",
  consoles: "src",
  protocol: "src",
  scriptNodes: "src",
  placers: "src",
  menus: "ui",
  views: "ui",
};

const NAME = /\/generated\/([A-Za-z]+)(?:\.ts)?$/;

const under = (file, dir) => file === dir || file.startsWith(dir + path.sep);

/** The plugin, or null when no product tree was given (the desktop's bundle). */
function productGenerated({ dir } = {}) {
  if (!dir) return null;
  const productTree = path.resolve(dir);
  return {
    name: "retroplug-product-generated",
    setup(build) {
      build.onResolve({ filter: /\/generated\/[A-Za-z]+(?:\.ts)?$/ }, (args) => {
        if (args.kind === "entry-point" || !args.importer) return undefined;
        const found = NAME.exec(args.path.split("\\").join("/"));
        if (!found || !Object.hasOwn(GENERATED, found[1])) return undefined;
        const importer = path.resolve(args.importer);
        if (!under(importer, path.join(SHELL, "src")) && !under(importer, path.join(SHELL, "ui"))) return undefined;
        const name = found[1];
        return { path: path.join(productTree, GENERATED[name], "generated", `${name}.ts`) };
      });
    },
  };
}

module.exports = { productGenerated };
````

- [ ] **Step 8: The tests: the plugin's plan, and the bundle checks**

`test/graph/plugin-product.test.ts` has three cases: the desktop places the controller and forces `midiMap` for a
model with one enabled; the plugin's plan (the shell's `buildGraph` bundled against the plugin's tree, in a Node
child) has no controller or surface node and leaves the cart at the user's own `midiSync` (E2); and a fresh plugin
project's settings have no `controller` key while a project carrying the block round-trips against its raw input (E8).
`bundle-split.mjs` takes a product name (it generates the product's tree into a temp directory and builds the three
product surfaces plus the UI from it) and removes it in a `finally`; `bundle-ui-split.test.ts` gains two cases: the
plugin's four bundles carry 0 modules under `packages/launchpad/` or `packages/lsdj-launchpad/` where the desktop's
carry 15, 15, 15 and 19, and the plugin's script entry registers no `rp.controller.session` and numbers
`rp.lsdj.serial-out` 22 (E6). `bundle-protocol.test.ts` gains the plugin's planner (2 modules, no node module).

Create `packages/retroplug/test/graph/plugin-product.test.ts`:

````ts
// A product without the Launchpad places no controller (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 8, E2). The
// plugin's product list carries neither the pack nor its placer, so a project whose `controller` section is enabled -
// written by the standalone, or by hand; the plugin's own submenu cannot enable it - has a model no placer claims:
// buildGraph places no surface-in, no session and no surface-out, and applies no sync override, so the cart syncs as
// its own settings say. On the desktop the same model places all three and forces the LSDj cart to `midiMap`, which is
// the positive control: a case that passed by the model being unreadable would fail there.
//
// The plugin's plan runs in a node child: buildGraph imports the generated placer table, so the product's plan is the
// shell's buildGraph bundled against the plugin's tree (as its own bundles are, through tools/product-generated.js).
import { test, expect } from "@retroplug/testing";
import { buildGraph, type GraphModel } from "../../src/graph/buildGraph";
import { parseConfig } from "../../src/projectConfig";

interface ByteStream {
  getReader(): { read(): Promise<{ done: boolean; value?: Uint8Array }> };
}
declare const tjs: {
  env: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  spawn(
    args: string[],
    opts: { stdout: "pipe"; stderr: "pipe" },
  ): {
    stdout: ByteStream | null;
    stderr: ByteStream | null;
    wait(): Promise<{ exit_status: number; term_signal: string | null }>;
  };
};

async function text(stream: ByteStream | null): Promise<string> {
  if (!stream) return "";
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  const reader = stream.getReader();
  for (;;) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    if (value) chunks.push(value);
  }
  let total = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) total += c.length;
  const all = new Uint8Array(total);
  let at = 0;
  for (const c of chunks) {
    all.set(c, at);
    at += c.length;
  }
  return new TextDecoder().decode(all);
}

/** The model both cases plan: one Game Boy running LSDj at the user's own MIDI-sync mode, and a controller enabled for
 *  it with the MI.MAP app (whose manifest sync override asks for `midiMap`). */
const MODEL = {
  systems: [
    {
      id: 1,
      platform: "gb",
      type: "rp.sameboy.gb",
      linkGroup: 0,
      exportMode: 0,
      resources: { rom: 1 },
      romName: "rom1",
      pipeline: [
        { kind: "lsdj-sync", node: "rp.lsdj.sync", config: { mode: "midiSync", tempoDivisor: 1, autoStart: false } },
      ],
    },
  ],
  routing: "stereo",
  shape: { kind: "multi", channels: 2 },
  midiRouting: "sendToAll",
  models: {
    controller: {
      app: "lsdj-midimap",
      target: "system",
      systemId: 0,
      appConfig: { quantise: "bar", follow: true, page: 0 },
      songRowTicks: [],
      anchor: null,
      cartSync: null,
    },
  },
};

function typesOf(model: unknown): { types: string[]; sync: { settings?: Record<string, unknown> } | null } {
  const built = buildGraph(model as GraphModel);
  const sync = built.document.nodes.find((node) => node.id === "sys-1/lsdj-sync");
  return {
    types: built.document.nodes.map((node) => node.type),
    sync: (sync as { settings?: Record<string, unknown> }) ?? null,
  };
}

test("the desktop places the controller for that model and forces the cart's sync mode", () => {
  // The positive control: the same model, the desktop's placers.
  const { types, sync } = typesOf(MODEL);
  expect(types.includes("rp.launchpad.surface-in")).toBe(true);
  expect(types.includes("rp.controller.session")).toBe(true);
  expect(types.includes("rp.launchpad.surface-out")).toBe(true);
  expect(sync?.settings?.mode).toBe("midiMap");
});

test("the plugin places no controller and no surface, and leaves the cart at the user's mode", async () => {
  const script =
    'const fs = require("fs"), os = require("os"), path = require("path");' +
    'const buildDir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "rp-plugin-plan-"));' +
    'require("../../packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs")' +
    '.generate({ root: path.resolve("../../"), product: "plugin", buildDir });' +
    'const product = path.join(buildDir, "products/plugin/packages/retroplug");' +
    'const esbuild = require("esbuild");' +
    'esbuild.build({ entryPoints: ["src/graph/buildGraph.ts"], bundle: true, format: "esm", platform: "neutral",' +
    ' mainFields: ["module", "main"], target: "es2020",' +
    ' tsconfigRaw: require("../../tools/ts-options").tsOptions({ alwaysStrict: true }),' +
    ' outfile: path.join(buildDir, "buildGraph.mjs"), nodePaths: [path.resolve("node_modules")],' +
    ' plugins: [require("../../tools/product-generated").productGenerated({ dir: product })].filter(Boolean) })' +
    '.then(() => import(require("url").pathToFileURL(path.join(buildDir, "buildGraph.mjs")).href))' +
    `.then((m) => { const built = m.buildGraph(${JSON.stringify(MODEL)});` +
    '  const sync = built.document.nodes.find((n) => n.id === "sys-1/lsdj-sync");' +
    '  fs.rmSync(buildDir, { recursive: true, force: true });' +
    '  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ types: built.document.nodes.map((n) => n.type),' +
    '    sync: sync ? sync.settings ?? null : null })); });';
  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "-e", script], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  if (status.term_signal || status.exit_status !== 0) throw new Error(`the plugin's plan failed: ${err || out}`);
  const plan = JSON.parse(out) as { types: string[]; sync: Record<string, unknown> | null };
  console.log(`# the plugin's plan: ${plan.types.join(", ")}; the cart's mode: ${String(plan.sync?.mode)}`);
  const placed = plan.types.filter((type) => type.startsWith("rp.controller.") || type.startsWith("rp.launchpad."));
  expect(placed).toEqual([]);
  // The cart follows the user's own setting, which the controller's override does not touch.
  expect(plan.sync?.mode).toBe("midiSync");
});

  // E8 and E5 in the product without the contributor (docs/modular-graph-phase-f5a-design.md section 8): the
  // `controller` section is a package's, so a product that carries no package contributing it has no default block to
  // write, and a block a project already carries is kept verbatim - never stripped, never rewritten, so a project
  // that goes back to the standalone loses nothing.

    schemaVersion: "5",

      layout: "grid",
      midiRouting: "sendToAll",
      audioRouting: "stereo",

        app: "lsdj-midimap",

  const desktop = parseConfig(JSON.stringify(raw));

    'require("../../packages/retroplug/scripts/lib/packages.mjs")' +
    '.generate({ root: path.resolve("../../"), product: "plugin", buildDir });' +
    'const product = path.join(buildDir, "products/plugin/packages/retroplug");' +
    'require("esbuild").build({ entryPoints: ["src/projectConfig.ts"], bundle: true, format: "esm",' +
    ' platform: "neutral", mainFields: ["module", "main"], target: "es2020",' +
    ' tsconfigRaw: require("../../tools/ts-options").tsOptions({ alwaysStrict: true }),' +
    ' outfile: path.join(buildDir, "projectConfig.mjs"), nodePaths: [path.resolve("node_modules")],' +
    ' plugins: [require("../../tools/product-generated").productGenerated({ dir: product })].filter(Boolean) })' +
    '.then(() => import(require("url").pathToFileURL(path.join(buildDir, "projectConfig.mjs")).href))' +
    `.then((m) => { const raw = ${JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(raw))};` +
    '  const parsed = m.parseConfig(raw);' +
    '  const written = m.serializeConfig(m.buildConfig(parsed.settings, parsed.systems));' +
    '  const fresh = JSON.stringify(m.buildConfig(m.DEFAULT_SETTINGS, []));' +
    '  fs.rmSync(buildDir, { recursive: true, force: true });' +
    '  process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ sections: Object.keys(m.defaultSections()),' +
    '    carries: Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(m.DEFAULT_SETTINGS.sections, "controller"),' +
    '    written, fresh })); });';
  const child = tjs.spawn([tjs.env.RP_NODE || "node", "-e", script], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  const [out, err, status] = await Promise.all([text(child.stdout), text(child.stderr), child.wait()]);
  if (status.term_signal || status.exit_status !== 0) throw new Error(`the plugin's project failed: ${err || out}`);
  const project = JSON.parse(out) as { sections: string[]; carries: boolean; written: string; fresh: string };
  console.log(`# the plugin's project sections: ${project.sections.join(", ") || "(none)"}`);
  expect(project.sections).toEqual([]);
  // E8: a FRESH project the plugin writes carries no `controller` key at all: no package in its list contributes the
  // section, so there is no default block for it to write.
  expect(project.carries).toBe(false);
  const fresh = JSON.parse(project.fresh) as { settings: Record<string, unknown> };
  expect(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(fresh.settings, "controller")).toBe(false);
  // E5: the project that carries one is written back byte for byte as the file had it, which is the whole of "kept":
  // the comparison is against the INPUT block, not against another build's re-serialisation.
  const written = JSON.parse(project.written) as { settings: Record<string, unknown> };
  expect(written.settings.controller).toEqual(raw.settings.controller);
  expect(written.settings).toEqual(raw.settings);
  // And the desktop reads the same block to the same thing, so "kept" is not the plugin's own idea of it.
  expect(desktop.settings.sections.controller).toEqual(raw.settings.controller);
});
````

````diff
+## 13. As built (the prototype)
+
+The prototype is five commits on the design commit `bef622dac`, one per stage, each built by DeepSeek Flash and reviewed by
+Opus (stage 4 in two halves), with each review's fix pass folded into the commit it belongs to by fixup and autosquash (the
+last pass split two hunks that belonged to stage 5 out of stage 4 and amended the tip's message), so the five trees stand
+as final and a stage report's sha is older than the branch's. **The shas in this section are the PROTOTYPE's:** `e9f92dc2d`,
+`c4292ebb5`, `a481a6cf1`, `4a7ff2c19` and stage 5, the commit that carries this section (so it cannot name its own sha: the
+tip of `proto/f5a-leftovers`). The whole prototype is 190 files, +6,352 -2,237 over the design commit (this section
+excluded), most of it stage 4's. Sections 1 to 11 above were corrected in place to what the build found; this section is
+the record of how, and the plan is written against it.
+
+**The stages**, by commit subject and current sha (files changed, lines added and removed):
+
+1. `e9f92dc2d fix(f5a): the app rows show what the app runs, and the UI joins one shell program` (14, +92 -69): the display
+   fix and `legacyConfigIndex` and `configRowCycler`'s index deleted, `hand-controller` re-recorded (E1),
+   `tsconfig.ui.json` folded, spec/07's stale lines and the audit doc's link.
+2. `c4292ebb5 feat(f5a): the N8 wire is a package of its own, and mesen no longer declares n8` (22, +164 -59):
+   `packages/n8-wire` with the reliable link moved and the three constants split out, `mesen` off `n8`, the lists, the
+   boundary fixtures.
+3. `a481a6cf1 feat(f5a): a package's views are their own module, apart from the menus` (47, +866 -339): `defineViews`,
+   `retroplug.views`, the generated `views.ts` with the moved checks, the `menuContributions` split, `lsdj`, `risa` and the
+   fixture moved, rule 3's and the generator's `ts/ui/` refusal, the three-part pure-tier proof.
+4. `4a7ff2c19 feat(f5a): the shell names no controller, and a contribution is manifest data` (106, +3,489 -1,357):
+   `projectSections`, `projectServices`, graph placers, the `project` host group, contribution kinds, the backend's harness
+   move, rule 9's lists and the generic native boundary rule.
+5. `59a9353ae feat(f5a): the plugin is its own product, and a bundle is a product's` (41, +1,821 -493): the `plugin` list, the generator's `--product`, the `onResolve` plugin, the product-supplied bundles, the
+   inverted `plugin.cmake` assertions, the per-product checks, E3, and the docs pass (the tip of `proto/f5a-leftovers`).
+
+**What each review found, and what the fix pass changed.**
+
+1. *Stage 1 (ready, no Critical).* The RED reproduced, E1 exactly one cycler, the fold an identical file set; 11 minors.
+   Controller decision: the display fix's fake-app case also pins a `toggle` knob defaulting false and a range clamp (the
+   review's option b). Fix pass (amending stage 1): both rows RED then green, spec/07's `:36` line restored with credits.
+2. *Stage 2 (with fixes, no Critical).* Important: the literal `n8-wire` include root in `n8`'s CMake was redundant and its
+   premise false (the twin's `INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES` genex is transitive; reproduced); six source comments still said mesen
+   declares `n8`. Minors: the device-ready claim (reworded to what is checked), a history comment, a column, the
+   `node-sdk-headers` link, an empty `transport/` directory. Fix pass: the root dropped and the twins rebuilt through the
+   link (images identical), the comments, the headers target.
+3. *Stage 3 (with fixes, no Critical).* Important: the pure proof did not bundle `menuDefs.ts`, so a re-import of a view
+   function passed everything (reproduced); no generator fixture ran a views-only package; `bundles.cmake`'s `BYPRODUCTS`
+   lacked `views.ts`. Fix pass: `menuDefs.ts` the third pure entry (RED: 315 modules), `zeta` views-only (RED with the
+   deletion off), the byproduct, one shared fixture alias map and the minors.
+4. *Stage 4, first half (with fixes, no Critical; the desktop unchanged over 464,192 `buildGraph` inputs and 390 round
+   trips, with E5 the one diff).* Important: an unstamped section read as current and could never migrate (decision 18);
+   `setSection` and `buildConfig` took core keys and `__proto__`; `placers.ts` missing from the byproducts; the planner
+   bundle test must refuse node modules by name; `Placement.wires` needs the node id. Sixteen minors. Fix pass folded into
+   the second half's commit.
+5. *Stage 4 as a whole (with fixes, no Critical; the desktop unchanged against the first half).* Important: the pack's
+   real kind check untested (a fixture copy stood in, and writing the test found the node-type check sitting after an
+   early return); `DirectGraph` no longer loaded the registry fill (an app's config parsed to `{}`, reproduced); nothing
+   guarded `buildGraph` against spelling a package's node type; `ControllerSyncRule` still in core; and the configure's
+   native check named the Launchpad. Fix pass (amending stage 4): the real check's own test, `DirectGraph`'s import, the
+   scanner's `DECLARED_NODE_TYPES` and package-prefix guard (RED on the pre-fix tree), the rule deleted from core, and the
+   GENERIC native boundary rule (decision 19) with its REDs on both halves.
+6. *Stage 5 and the whole prototype (with fixes).* **Critical:** `pnpm typecheck` created `build/` (the plugin's tree), so
+   CI's own order, a typecheck and then `./build.sh`, skipped the configure and failed on `could not load cache`
+   (reproduced; the parallel kit ran on a configured `build/` and could not see it). Important: the CLI bundle, SDK assets
+   and example sessions lost their ordering on the generator; `$<TARGET_OBJECTS:t>` passed unjudged (stage 4's message
+   said otherwise); a `PACKAGES` product matching no list failed at build; the design contradicted the tree on the twin and
+   lacked E8; the guides still described `defineUi({ views })`, the controller group and two item 8s; the harness target
+   sat before the device return. Fifteen minors. Last fix pass (fixups folded by autosquash into the stages that
+   introduced each defect; no golden, baseline, digest, image or pack byte moved): the typecheck's tree under
+   `packages/retroplug/.products/` and `build.sh` / `build.bat` testing `build/CMakeCache.txt` (RED on a scratch extract,
+   then a fresh-tree real configure), the generator ordering restored, objects judged (`objects` and `objects-declared`),
+   an unlisted `PACKAGES` refused at configure with a held fixture project, the docs, the narrower vouchers, an object
+   library per bundle set, and the comment rewraps.
+
+**Departures from the design as committed (`bef622dac`), and why.** Each is also corrected in place above.
+
+- **The E1 step list rotates** (3.1): the recorder steps from the row's own index; and the recorded case's own comment and
+  the audit doc's prose were corrected, since both asserted the old reading.
+- **No `n8-wire` in the export tool's list, and no literal include root** (4.2): the tool calls no `retroplug_package()`,
+  and the twin's genex is transitive. **A header-only manifest, not a refused-manifest case**, and the boundary fixtures
+  are `refused-native/` and `read/` (a link boundary is a target property). The wire links `node-sdk-headers`.
+- **The pure proof has three entries, and the generator's fixture tree puts its UI module under `ts/ui/`** (5.2, 5.4).
+  `ViewsContribution.views` is required.
+- **An unstamped section reads as version 1** (6.1, decision 18); **`setSection`, `section` and `buildConfig` refuse core
+  keys and `__proto__`, and a hand-edited `__proto__` key is kept as data** (6.1).
+- **The section's parse is hand-written, and the pack's control modules are in `ts/control/`** (6.1, 6.5, decision 25).
+- **`ControllerSyncRule` is in the pack's placer alone, `Placement.wires` takes the node id, and `PlaceSpec` is core's
+  structural type** (6.3).
+- **The kind has no `idOf`, refuses an app-member name, takes the pack's whole validation in its `check`, and `nodeTypes`
+  is the wired set** (6.5, decision 23): a type the graph does not wire is refused where the old generator accepted it.
+- **The registry is filled by a side-effect import in `DirectGraph` and `projectConfig`,** not by `accept` alone (6.3).
+- **The role-golden runner alone translates `model.controller`** (6.3); `build-graph.test.ts` needs none.
+- **`SHELL_IMPORTS` gains `core/defineKind`, `core/placer` and `tracker/projectService`** and loses `tracker/trackerPlayback`
+  (6.6); the stage 4 report said `trackerPlayback` was never listed, and the diff shows it removed.
+- **The native boundary rule is generic, not a configure check naming the Launchpad** (6.7, decision 19): the design's RED
+  could not run as written because the check exempted a shell outright. `native`'s `devDependencies` gain `launchpad`,
+  `n8`, `device-io` and `devtest`, and three targets are vouched for where they are made (`retroplug-ts-packages`,
+  `retroplug-box-usb-cdc`, `retroplug` against the plugin's list).
+- **The harness target links `node-sdk-headers` and is declared below the device early-return** (6.7).
+- **The alias claim was confirmed, so the `onResolve` plugin** (7.2, decision 17); **a product's tree resolves through a
+  `paths` file and `nodePaths`,** and `bundleInputs` is async (decision 24).
+- **No `LIST` default; a bundle set is the list's content; an unlisted `PACKAGES` is refused at configure** (7.2,
+  decision 21); the bundles' CMake is `packages/native/cmake/product-bundles.cmake` and one OBJECT library per set.
+- **`product-lists.mjs` exists because CMake cannot enumerate a JSON object's keys** (7.1); the subsequence rule refuses a
+  duplicate by name and is a function so a fixture can hold it; `order()` skips the shell for a non-desktop list only.
+- **The typecheck's tree is `packages/retroplug/.products/`, not `build/`,** and one `tsc` runs per non-desktop list the
+  manifest names (7.2, decision 22). **`--product-dir` is one form in all three build scripts.**
+- **E3 was applied by hand to the committed formatting** (7.3): the dump's writer re-indents the whole file. The stage 5
+  review checked the dump parses to exactly the committed file.
+- **E8 is an edge** (8, decision 20), and spec/06's "Adding a package" is restructured to items 1 to 13 (the kinds' item
+  pushes the rest down) with the section, service, placer and kind rules stated rather than cited.
+- **Stage 4's sections are one commit built in two halves,** as the design said; the controller decisions of the stage 4
+  review (decisions 18 to 20) correct 6.1, 6.7 and section 8.
+
+**Behaviour edges as built.** E1: `hand-controller`'s `lp-app-quantise` cycler only (index, value and the rotated steps;
+no other recorded case moved). E2: the plugin's plan places no controller node and no sync override, held by the
+planner case against the plugin's own tree and not by a run of an old plugin (the real-plugin render is acceptance's). E3:
+the registration golden's `retroplug` row loses two types. E4: the plugin's bundles shrink by 20,326 (control plane),
+48,384 (UI), 21,257 (render worker) and 38,445 (script nodes) bytes, the first three moved by +9, +9 and +11 comment bytes
+on the desktop's side since the first measurement (-20,317, -48,375, -21,246). E5: `futureSetting` is kept, the one test

+by no test. E8: a fresh plugin project has no `controller` block, held against its input. E1 to E8 are all recorded;
+no audio, graph document of a product listing the Launchpad, or saved-file shape moved.
+

+(`.superpowers/verify/tip-verify-par.sh`), every leg exit 0 with no retry, with `pnpm sdl:controller` run alone (`SDL
````

````text
  ok: nothing selected, nothing claimed; unclaimed, the device's notes reach the shared stream

  ok: a second standalone leaves the first one's device alone, and does not hear its pads
````

- [ ] **Step 3: The serial kit, whole, and its legs**

The kit is `.superpowers/verify/tip-verify.sh`, the same legs the parallel script runs, in the same order, one at a
time. Write it to a scratch path of its own (never into the repository), run it with `TVL` naming the log prefix, and
keep both the summary and every leg's log: the figures below are the final verification's, and a difference is a
finding except where the rules above say otherwise. The script is quoted whole because the set of legs IS the
acceptance, and its `HERE` makes `norm-sha.sh` and `measure.sh` the kit's own.

````bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tip-verify.sh: the SERIAL full verification run, root-relative and timed.
#
#   TV_ROOT=<repo>      the tree to verify (default: the repo this script lives in, ../..)
#   TVL=<prefix>        the log prefix (summary: <prefix>-summary.txt, legs: <prefix>-<leg>.log)
#   TV_SKIP_SDLCTL=1    skip the sdlctl leg (it claims system-wide ALSA MIDI ports)
#
# Every leg's summary line is "<leg> exit <code> <secs>s", so the "<leg> exit <code>" prefix existing greps use is
# untouched. Every leg runs under `nice -n 19 ionice -c3` (a shared box), inherited by its children. Scratch dirs are
# unique per run.
set -uo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
TV_ROOT="${TV_ROOT:-$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)}"
export TV_ROOT
cd "$TV_ROOT" || exit 2
L=${TVL:-/tmp/tv-verify}
RES=${RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR:-/workspaces/resources}
run() {
  local n=$1; shift
  local start end rc
  start=$(date +%s)
  nice -n 19 ionice -c3 "$@" > "$L-$n.log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  end=$(date +%s)
  echo "$n exit $rc $((end - start))s" >> "$L-summary.txt"
}
: > "$L-summary.txt"

run build cmake --build build -j$(nproc)
run typecheck pnpm typecheck
run test pnpm test
run plugin pnpm test:plugin
run egfix env RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR="$RES" build/bin/retroplug-engine-graph-test
run parity env RP_FAIL_ON_SKIP=1 RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR="$RES" pnpm test:native parity
run native env RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR="$RES" pnpm test:native
run nativeci env RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/nonexistent-rp-resources RISA_SRC=/nonexistent-rp-risa pnpm test:native
run ui env RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR="$RES" pnpm test:ui
run node pnpm test:node
run clits pnpm test:cli-ts
run docs pnpm check:docs
run n8 pnpm test:n8
S="suppressions=$PWD/packages/native/test/sanitizer/tsan.supp halt_on_error=1"
run tsanbuild cmake --build build-tsan --target retroplug-engine-graph-test retroplug-graph-test retroplug-n8-test -j$(nproc)

run rendertests bash -c 'for t in audio-render render-guard risa-render risa-render-hff risa-render-region sms-render; do RETROPLUG_RESOURCES_DIR=/workspaces/resources pnpm test:native $t || exit 1; done'
````

````text
  CMakeFiles/n8_host_trap_probe.dir/workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/packages/graph-runtime/device-check/trap-probe.cpp.o: in function `main':
  /workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/packages/graph-runtime/device-check/trap-probe.cpp:11:(.text.startup.main+0x4): undefined reference to `__wrap__Znwj'
  /workspaces/RetroPlug-main/cuttlefish/packages/graph-runtime/device-check/trap-probe.cpp:12:(.text.startup.main+0x14): undefined reference to `__wrap_malloc'
````

and the image's sizes: `== pio: flash 199536, data 46120, bss 120600 bytes; 191960 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 245656 bytes into flash; RAM 358704 bytes in all` and `== native: flash 199920, data 32084, bss 114368 bytes; 192344 of the flash runs from RAM; the load image ends 232004 bytes into flash; RAM 338824 bytes in all`.

An image carries the day it was built: the Pico SDK's standard binary info stamps it with `__DATE__`
(`pico_standard_binary_info`, since nothing sets `PICO_NO_BI_PROGRAM_BUILD_DATE`), once, a fixed-length string. So the
check counts that string (it must be exactly one) and hashes a copy with it normalised to 4 November 2026, as
`.superpowers/verify/norm-sha.sh` normalises it for the baseline's and every stage's run; nothing else may differ, and
the sizes the device scripts print do not move with the date. The bytes also rest on the build's inputs, so a hash
compares only an image built from this worktree's path, against the same SDK checkouts (`/opt/pico-sdk` for the check,
`/workspaces/pico-sdk` for the box), the same Pico-PIO-USB checkout (`/workspaces/Pico-PIO-USB`) and
`arm-none-eabi-g++` 13.2.1.

- [ ] **Step 9: E2 on the real plugin: a recorded manual item, said plainly**

Design section 13 asks acceptance for a Reaper render of an LSDj project whose saved state carries
`controller.enabled: true`, showing the cart following MIDI clock rather than being forced into `midiMap`. **No
existing harness can do it without new tooling.** The render fixtures are authored by `tools/author-lsdj-rplg.js`,
whose TS half (`test-native/author-lsdj-rplg.ts`) builds a project through the stores and sets the LSDj role's sync
mode; it has no option for the project's `controller` section, and the only other door is patching the exported
`.rplg`'s project JSON, which is new tooling. So this is a recorded MANUAL item, not an invented harness, and the plan
is explicit about it: 1. Build a drift fixture (`node tools/author-lsdj-rplg.js midi-drift`), which authoring writes
with the desktop's default `controller` block, `enabled: false`. 2. Open it in the standalone (`retroplug-sdl`) and
enable the control surface in the project (`Control Surface > Enabled`, target `system`) with no device attached, then
save. This is the by-hand step the item exists for; nothing here opens a port, because no pair is claimed while the
surface is disabled and none is connected. 3. Render the existing drift project against that saved state and analyze
it: `tools/run-reaper-render.sh examples/reaper/lsdj_midi_drift.rpp <the saved .rplg.zip>` then
`tools/reaper-timing-analyze.py build/reaper-lsdj-midi-drift.wav --drift`. 4. What it asserts: the drift verdict is
the leg's own PASS. An old plugin, which placed the controller and forced the cart to `midiMap` for an enabled
section, would stop the cart following the DAW's clock, so the per-beat transients the analyzer pairs with ReaSynth's
clicks would not line up and the analysis fails. The plan claims no figure for this run: no log records it, and it is
not in CI.

- [ ] **Step 11: The bundle module diff, base against tip**

The desktop's control plane and UI bundles legitimately GAIN the pack's control-plane modules (Task 4 moved the
controller into the pack, and the desktop lists it), so the phase's bundling proof is a module-by-module diff rather
than a count: the same recorder over a `git archive` of the design commit and over this tree, and every added and
removed module named. `tools/build-session.js`'s `bundleInputs(entry, format)` bundles in memory and returns every
module that went in; `tools/build-ui.js` exports the same instrument for the UI. Both are async at this tree (a
product's redirect is a plugin), and the recorder awaits them, which also works on the design commit's sync form. The
recorder, whole:

````js
// Records, per bundle, the modules esbuild put in: the F5a bundle diff (Task 6's leg).
//
//   node bundle-modules.mjs <tree> <out.json>
//
// The build-session entries resolve against packages/retroplug (the repo's own bundle tests run there), so the recorder
// changes there before it loads the tree's esbuild. `bundleInputs` is SYNC at the design commit and ASYNC from Task 5
// (a product's redirect is an esbuild plugin, which `buildSync` refuses), so every call is awaited.
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { chdir } from "node:process";
import { mkdirSync, realpathSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";

const tree = resolve(process.argv[2]);
const outFile = resolve(process.argv[3] ?? "/tmp/f5a-bundles/modules.json");
const ENTRIES = [
  ["cp", "src/pluginControlPlane.ts", "esm"],
  ["worker", "src/render/worker.ts", "iife"],
  ["sdk", "cli/sdk.ts", "esm"],
  ["cli", "cli/cli.ts", "esm"],
  ["planner", "src/graph/protocolNodes.ts", "esm"],
  ["script-nodes", "src/generated/scriptNodes.ts", "iife"],
];
chdir(`${tree}/packages/retroplug`);
const require = createRequire(`${tree}/packages/retroplug/`);
const { bundleInputs } = require(`${tree}/tools/build-session.js`);
const REAL = realpathSync(tree);
// A module outside the tree (a symlinked submodule's own node_modules) is named by its `deps/...` tail, so the two
// trees' lists compare: their roots differ, and a resolved path through a submodule symlink leaves the tree.
const norm = (p) => {
  const rel = relative(REAL, resolve(p)).split(sep).join("/");
  if (!rel.startsWith("../")) return rel;
  const at = rel.indexOf("/deps/");
  return at >= 0 ? rel.slice(at + 1) : rel;
};
const out = {};
for (const [name, entry, format] of ENTRIES) {
  const r = await bundleInputs(entry, format);
  out[name] = { modules: r.inputs.length, inputs: r.inputs.map(norm).sort() };
}
const ui = require(`${tree}/tools/build-ui.js`);
const r = await ui.bundleInputs(`${tree}/packages/retroplug/ui/main.tsx`);
out.ui = { modules: r.inputs.length, inputs: r.inputs.map(norm).sort() };
mkdirSync(resolve(outFile, ".."), { recursive: true });
writeFileSync(outFile, JSON.stringify(out, null, 1) + "\n");
console.log(`recorded ${Object.keys(out).length} bundles to ${outFile}`);
````

- [ ] **Step 12: What is owed**

These are the phase's debts, recorded so nothing thinks they ran:

- **Windows**: the build and `test.bat` (all four suites) through the user's Windows agent, and `reaper:win` with
  the two Windows Reaper checks. The new `n8-wire` CMake, the per-list bundle targets with their long
  `build/products/plugin/...` paths, `product-lists.mjs` through `execute_process`, the OBJECT libraries and the
  per-format C arrays under `/W4 /WX`, and `build.bat`'s `CONFIGURED` have not seen MSVC.
- **macOS and the arm64 Linux CI job**: neither has built these packages or the product trees. The exact-byte
  oracles refuse a foreign host rather than comparing a tree with itself (`RP_PARITY_REQUIRE_TARGET`,
  `RP_KIT_GOLDEN_REQUIRE_TARGET`, `RP_RENDER_GOLDEN_REQUIRE_TARGET`), so their first run must set those flags and
  report, not quietly pass.
- **CI**: `build.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch`, pull requests and pushes to `main` only, so F5a's first CI run is
  a dispatched run or a PR the user starts. It is also the first place the typecheck-then-`./build.sh` order runs
  for real (Step 2 holds it locally).
- **E2's real-plugin render** (Step 9): a recorded manual item, because no harness writes a `.rplg` with
  `controller.enabled: true`.
- **The per-header device check** for a header-only package (`n8-wire`'s link is device-ready by inspection), and
  **a typecheck of the shell against a non-desktop generated tree** (the shell program resolves `generated/*` to the
  desktop's, design 11.5).
- **A `component` view drawn on a real host** (F4c's, unchanged), **`host.kits`**, **gamepad axis tokens**,
  **`MemoryType`**, **the view reopen key**, **downloadable packs**, and **F5b** (the SDL standalone's audio and
  MIDI as packages behind generic backend interfaces), which is the split's remaining phase.
- **The `controlSurface` user-config block and the `config` host group** name the concept and import nothing; F5a
  leaves them (design section 11, item 1).
